The network names come from meraki_network_info: run the meraki-networks job for the network variable and the joins.

items.title: Known caveats
items.text:
• The uplink metrics are validated against the simulator only (see above).
  • Devices without a name have no name label on meraki_device_info: Tapyr leaves out empty label values, as Prometheus does.
  • meraki-wireless-client-counts needs access points; organizations without wireless return no item.
  • Networks bound to configuration templates are reported as returned by the API.

items.title: End-to-end test
items.text:
TAPYR_E2E_MERAKI_API_KEY=... go test -tags e2e -run TestMerakiDashboard ./test/e2e/

It runs every template once against the organizations of the key (a read-only key is enough, for example the one of a DevNet sandbox), checks that the organization, network and device samples have the expected shape and that the device jobs succeed, and spends one request per organization and template, plus one for the organizations. A key generated a minute before can still be refused (401): wait a little and run it again.

items.title: teltonika-rms
items.text:
Teltonika Remote Management System (RMS) cloud API: status, mobile signal and data usage of the devices managed in RMS.

Validation status: tested against the real platform (November 2026, RMS API v3-BETA), and against the simulator in CI. The RMS API is in beta: Teltonika announces additive changes that may still break clients.

items.title: Coverage
items.text:
Template Endpoint Default interval Requests Metrics rms-devices GET /devices (offset pagination, 100 per page, fields selected) 5m 1 per 100 devices rms_device_up, rms_device_last_connection_timestamp_seconds, rms_device_last_update_timestamp_seconds, rms_device_uptime_seconds, rms_device_temperature_celsius, rms_device_mobile_rssi_dbm, rms_device_mobile_rsrp_dbm, rms_device_mobile_rsrq_db, rms_device_mobile_sinr_db, rms_device_mobile_connected, rms_device_mobile_roaming, rms_device_info, rms_device_mobile_info, rms_devices rms-device-data-usage GET /devices/{id}/data-usage for today (UTC), one instance per device 6h 1 per device rms_device_mobile_received_bytes_today, rms_device_mobile_transmitted_bytes_today
  • The device list carries the mobile fields of the first modem (signal, RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, operator, connection type and state, home or roaming), so the radio metrics cost no extra request. The fields of a second modem (*_2) are not collected yet.
  • rms_device_up is 1 for status 1 (online), 0 for offline (0, null) and pending (2).
  • The mobile states are gauges: rms_device_mobile_connected is 1 when connection_state is Connected, rms_device_mobile_roaming is 1 when network_state is Roaming (0 for Home or Searching). rms_device_mobile_info keeps the operator and the connection type, and is absent while the device has no service (operator N/A).
  • Data usage values are today's totals since 00:00 UTC per modem and SIM (window values exposed as gauges, see ADR 0009); a device without usage today has no sample.
  • Device identifiers are the RMS id, in the device_id label of every device metric; the data usage metrics also carry modem and sim. rms_device_info carries the name, serial, model, firmware and company, to join with * on (device_id) group_left (name) rms_device_info.
  • RMS shows what devices report, at their own monitoring interval (dynamic_monitoring, often 300 seconds). Polling the device list faster than that only spends quota: the default interval is 5 minutes.

items.title: Auth setup
items.text:
1. In RMS, enable two-factor authentication on the account (required for tokens).
  2. Account settings > API > Access tokens: create a personal access token with the devices:read scope. It is shown once.
  3. Give it to Tapyr as the token secret, for example from an environment variable (see examples/rms.yaml).

items.title: Limits
items.text:
Limit Value Source monthly (quota) 100000 requests per month; max: auto, synced from X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset Documented: RMS web API ("100 000 requests per month", 429 with Retry-After). Measured on 2026-11-03: the headers are present on every response (not documented), and the reset was one month after the first request of the window, not the start of a calendar month; the reset header sets the window end rate 2 requests per second, burst 4, per token Assumed: no rate is documented concurrency 2 concurrent requests per token Assumed

Quota maths: 100000 requests a month is about 3300 a day. With the defaults, rms-devices spends 288 requests a day per 100 devices; rms-device-data-usage adds 4 per device and day. tapyr plan shows the projection.

The quota is scoped by credential: accounts sharing a token share it. If other tools use the same token, give Tapyr a share of it (budget.share).

items.title: Simulator
items.text:
tapyr sim --provider teltonika-rms --listen 127.0.0.1:8084

8084 is the port of the simulator under tapyr sim --all --listen-base 127.0.0.1:8081 (portOffset: 3). The fixtures follow the shape of anonymized recordings of the real API (tapyr record), over a synthetic fleet of 12 devices whose status, signal and temperature move over simulated time. The simulator accepts the token sim-rms-token, enforces the limits above and sends the three X-RateLimit-* headers.

Scenario Effect default No fault quota-tight 3000 requests left in the month, another client spending 20 an hour bad-day From 1h, slow responses (p50 800 ms, p99 6 s) for an hour; from 2h, 30% of /devices requests fail with 503 for 30 minutes; at 4h, a 10-minute outage

items.title: Dashboard
items.text: dashboards/teltonika-rms.json (Grafana, Prometheus data source, model variable): fleet status, offline and stale devices, roaming, temperature, mobile signal, data usage, monthly quota (limit, used by Tapyr and by others, remaining, from Tapyr self-metrics).

items.title: Known caveats
items.text:
• The API is a beta: field names may change; tapyr provider lint and the e2e test catch it.
  • Only the first modem is collected.
  • last_connection_at and last_update_at are parsed as UTC, as documented.
  • The monthly quota window is learned from the reset header; before the first response, Tapyr assumes a calendar month.

items.title: End-to-end test
items.text:
TAPYR_E2E_RMS_TOKEN=... go test -tags e2e -run TestTeltonikaRMS ./test/e2e/

It lists the devices once, checks that the samples have the expected shape and that the quota headers are learned, and spends one request per 100 devices plus one data-usage request per device.

items.title: teltonika-rutos
items.text:
Local REST API of Teltonika routers running RutOS: system, mobile modems, interfaces and failover, polled on each router.

Validation status: built from the official OpenAPI descriptions of the RutOS API (7.6 to 7.26.1), tested against a real router (Teltonika CAP7xx, RutOS 07.24.5, November 2026: every template, 30 metric families, login and logout) and against the simulator in CI. The documentation describes load as percentages; the router reports load averages (0.42), which the metrics expose as such.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• RutOS 07.06 or later (the REST API does not exist before; Teltonika community). The legacy ubus JSON-RPC API is not supported.
  • A RutOS user, ideally in a group whose ACL grants read access only (GET requests map to the read permission).
  • HTTPS access from Tapyr to the router (the default from 07.12 on RUTX and 07.15 on other models). Routers use self-signed certificates: give Tapyr their certificates with tls.caFile, or set tls.insecureSkipVerify: true explicitly (logged as a warning).

items.title: Coverage
items.text:
Template Endpoint Default interval Requests Metrics rutos-system GET /api/system/device/usage/status 1m 1 per router rutos_system_uptime_seconds, rutos_system_load1, rutos_system_load5, rutos_system_load15 (load averages), rutos_memory_total_bytes, rutos_memory_free_bytes, rutos_flash_total_bytes, rutos_flash_free_bytes rutos-device GET /api/system/device/status 30m 1 per router rutos_device_info (model, product code, firmware, hostname, serial, hardware revision) rutos-modems GET /api/modems/status 1m 1 per router rutos_modem_connected, rutos_modem_rssi_dbm, rutos_modem_rsrp_dbm, rutos_modem_rsrq_db, rutos_modem_sinr_db, rutos_modem_signal_quality_ratio, rutos_modem_temperature_celsius, rutos_modem_received_bytes_total, rutos_modem_transmitted_bytes_total, rutos_modem_registered, rutos_modem_roaming, rutos_modem_sim_inserted, rutos_modem_active_sim, rutos_modem_info (model, operator, network type, band) rutos-interfaces GET /api/interfaces/status 1m 1 per router rutos_interface_up, rutos_interface_uptime_seconds, rutos_interface_received_bytes_total, rutos_interface_transmitted_bytes_total, rutos_interface_received_packets_total, rutos_interface_transmitted_packets_total, rutos_interface_info rutos-failover GET /api/failover/status 1m 1 per router rutos_failover_interface_online, rutos_failover_interface_enabled, rutos_failover_interface_score, rutos_failover_interface_lost_probes
  • Every sample has a router label: the name of the target.
  • Memory and flash sizes are reported by RutOS in MB and converted to bytes.
  • Offline modems (no SIM, disabled) are skipped.
  • The signal quality computed by RutOS (a percentage) is exposed as a ratio from 0 to 1.
  • States that change go to gauges, not to rutos_modem_info: rutos_modem_registered (1 registered on a network, home or roaming), rutos_modem_roaming (1 roaming), rutos_modem_sim_inserted (1 when RutOS reports the SIM Inserted) and rutos_modem_active_sim (the SIM slot in use, 1 or 2).
  • RutOS renamed some modem fields in 7.12 (signal to rssi, oper to operator, state to data_conn_state, netstate to operator_state); the templates read the new names and fall back to the old ones.
  • Interface and modem byte counters are native counters (type: counter): they reset when the router reboots, which rate() handles.

items.title: Auth setup
items.text:
Give Tapyr the username and password of the RutOS user as secrets, and the address of each router as the baseURL param of its target (see examples/rutos.yaml).

session_login: POST /api/login with the username and password answers a bearer token valid 5 minutes (api_session_timeout, 300 seconds by default). Tapyr keeps one session per router (perTarget), renews it 30 seconds before it expires and logs the replaced session out (POST /api/logout), and logs out every session when it stops: RutOS keeps sessions open after their token expires and its memory grows when a client logs in repeatedly (Teltonika community).

items.title: Limits
items.text:
Limit Value Source rate 2 requests per second per router, burst 2 Assumed: no limit is documented, routers are resource-constrained concurrency 2 concurrent requests per router Assumed

With the default intervals, a router answers about 4 requests per minute plus a login every 4.5 minutes.

items.title: Simulator
items.text:
tapyr sim --provider teltonika-rutos --listen 127.0.0.1:8085

8085 is the port of the simulator under tapyr sim --all --listen-base 127.0.0.1:8081 (portOffset: 4). The simulator serves one router (a RUTX50 with a 5G modem, a second modem without SIM, LAN, wired WAN and a mobile backup in the failover) under /api, with values moving over simulated time. It accepts the login sim-user / sim-password, issues 5-minute tokens and serves the logout. Every target of an account reaches the same simulated router.

Scenario Effect default No fault quota-tight RutOS has no quota: a router at the limit of its resources, slow (p50 1.5 s, p99 8 s) and answering 20% of the requests with 503 bad-day At 1h, the router reboots: 5 minutes without answer, then every session opened before is rejected; from 2h, half of the modem requests fail with 500 for 30 minutes

items.title: Dashboard
items.text: dashboards/teltonika-rutos.json (Grafana, Prometheus data source, router variable): uptime, load average, memory and flash, router inventory, mobile signal and throughput, interface throughput, failover state. RutOS has no quota: the dashboard has no API quota row.

items.title: Known caveats
items.text:
• Payloads may change between firmware versions; the e2e test and tapyr provider lint catch it for the versions tested.
  • tls.caFile applies to the account: one bundle holding the certificates of every router of the account.

items.title: End-to-end test
items.text:
TAPYR_E2E_RUTOS_URL=https://192.0.2.10 TAPYR_E2E_RUTOS_USERNAME=... TAPYR_E2E_RUTOS_PASSWORD=... \
  go test -tags e2e -run TestTeltonikaRutOS ./test/e2e/

It runs every template once against the router (certificate verification skipped unless TAPYR_E2E_RUTOS_CA_FILE is set) and checks that the samples have the expected shape and that the login succeeds.

items.title: unifi-site-manager
items.text:
UniFi Site Manager API v1, the cloud API of Ubiquiti: the consoles, sites, devices and ISP metrics of every console of a UI account, with one API key. It suits a fleet of consoles (an MSP, several offices): one key reads them all through api.ui.com, without access to each console.

Validation status: real platform. Run against a real UI account on 2026-11-13, strictly read-only, with an API key limited to the Site Manager scope: one console (UniFi OS 5.1, UniFi Network 10.6) with two WAN interfaces. The hosts, sites, devices and 5-minute ISP metrics templates ran with tapyr run, and the units were checked against the UniFi interface. The hourly ISP metrics endpoint was called but not run as a job, and the pagination over several pages is simulator-only (the account has one console). The package is built from the Getting Started page and the OpenAPI description (Site Manager API 1.0.0).

Not covered: the local API of the consoles, and the old session API of the UniFi Network application (which UniFi Poller reads, with the detail of each client and port). This package gives the cloud view of the fleet.

items.title: Coverage
items.text:
Template Endpoint Default interval Requests Metrics unifi-hosts GET /v1/hosts 15m 1 per 100 consoles unifi_host_info (type, name, model, version, release channel), unifi_host_connected, unifi_host_blocked, unifi_host_state_change_timestamp_seconds, unifi_host_last_backup_timestamp_seconds unifi-sites GET /v1/sites 5m 1 per 100 sites unifi_site_info (name, timezone, gateway model), unifi_site_devices and unifi_site_devices_offline (by kind: gateway, wifi, wired), unifi_site_devices_pending_update, unifi_site_clients (wifi, wired), unifi_site_guest_clients, unifi_site_critical_notifications, unifi_site_internet_issues, unifi_site_internet_uptime_ratio, unifi_site_wifi_tx_retry_ratio; per WAN interface: unifi_site_wan_up, unifi_site_wan_uptime_ratio, unifi_site_wan_info (ISP name and ASN) unifi-devices GET /v1/devices 5m 1 per 100 consoles unifi_device_info (name, model, product line, version, firmware status, console), unifi_device_up, unifi_device_update_available, unifi_device_boot_timestamp_seconds unifi-isp-metrics GET /v1/isp-metrics/5m?beginTimestamp=<now - 1h> 5m 1 Per site and WAN interface, in 5-minute windows: unifi_isp_latency_avg_seconds, unifi_isp_latency_max_seconds, unifi_isp_packet_loss_ratio, unifi_isp_uptime_ratio, unifi_isp_expected_download_bits_per_second, unifi_isp_expected_upload_bits_per_second (label period="5m") unifi-isp-metrics-hourly GET /v1/isp-metrics/1h?beginTimestamp=<now - 4h> 1h 1 The same metrics in hourly windows (label period="1h"), optional
  • ISP metrics are published late. The 5-minute windows reach the API about 30 minutes after they end (2 to 3 hours for the hourly ones). Each run reads the last hour (4 hours for the hourly template), and every sample carries the start of its window (metricTime) as its source timestamp. The windows already sent are deduplicated: a 5-minute job sends about one new window per run, and a missed run leaves no gap.
  • The expected speeds are configured, not measured. download_kbps and upload_kbps of the ISP metrics are the expected ISP speeds set on the WAN interface in UniFi Network (Settings > Internet, the expected ISP speeds of the WAN). They are neither the traffic nor the result of a speed test, and they stay constant until someone changes them (checked on a real account).
  • Units. The latency is in milliseconds in the API (seconds here), the uptime and the packet loss are integer percentages (ratios here). downtime is not mapped: its unit is not documented, and the real account only showed zeros.
  • WAN interfaces are named after their interface (wan, wan2), as the API gives them, never after the name or the ISP set by the user; the ISP of each is in unifi_site_wan_info.
  • Devices are those of the consoles where the account is owner or super admin (as documented). Their identifier (device_id) is the device MAC address, as the API names it. Descriptive attributes are in unifi_device_info; no IP address and no note (free text) are collected.
  • Not collected: the public address of the consoles and of the WAN interfaces, MAC addresses of consoles and gateways, serial numbers, the location of the consoles, the owner (email, name) and the free-text description of the sites, all present in the responses. No client is collected (the API gives counts only).
  • Not covered yet: the SD-WAN configurations and their status (/v1/sd-wan-configs, one request per configuration), and the connector (/v1/connector/consoles/{id}/...), which reaches the local APIs of a console and also accepts writes.

items.title: Auth setup
items.text:
The API authenticates with an API key in the X-API-Key header.

  1. Sign in to unifi.ui.com with an account that owns or administers the consoles.
  2. Open Settings > API Keys and create a key. Keep only the Site Manager scope: the UniFi Applications scope also manages the settings of Network and Protect, which Tapyr never needs. Pick an expiration that suits your rotation.
  3. Copy the key (it is shown once) and give it to Tapyr as the apiKey secret (see examples/unifi.yaml).

The key sees every console of the account. To collect a subset, use another account with access to that subset only.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
Limit Value Source rate 10,000 requests a minute, per API key (assumed scope) Getting Started, Rate Limiting
  • The documentation gives the rate per API version (10,000 a minute for the v1 stable release, 100 for Early Access endpoints, which no template uses) without its scope: the package assumes it is per key (credential). Accounts sharing a key share it.
  • Exceeded, the API answers 429 with Retry-After in seconds, which Tapyr follows. No quota header is sent (checked on a real account), so there is nothing to sync.
  • The connector has its own limit (100 requests a minute per console), unused by the package.

With the defaults, an account with up to 100 consoles spends 4 requests every 5 minutes and one every 15 minutes, about one request a minute: the limit is never in sight.

items.title: Simulator
items.text:
tapyr sim --provider unifi-site-manager --listen 127.0.0.1:8088

8088 is the port of the simulator under tapyr sim --all --listen-base 127.0.0.1:8081 (portOffset: 7). A synthetic account of 3 consoles, each with one site and 6 devices (a gateway, 2 switches, 3 access points), one site with two WAN interfaces, in the response shapes of the OpenAPI description and of the real responses. It accepts the key sim-unifi-key, enforces the rate limit, and serves ISP windows published late (30 minutes for 5-minute windows, 3 hours for hourly ones).

Known gaps of the simulator: the cursor of the API is in the body (nextToken), which the cursor pagination of the simulator does not serve, so the fixtures of the lists paginate themselves, 2 consoles a page, whatever pageSize asks; the ISP metrics fixture returns the windows of the range the templates request, whatever beginTimestamp says.

Scenario Effect default No fault quota-tight Other integrations of the account spend most of the rate limit: a quarter of the requests get 429 bad-day From 1h, slow responses (p50 800 ms, p99 5 s) for an hour; from 2h, 30% of the ISP metrics requests fail with 502 for 30 minutes; at 4h, a 10-minute outage

items.title: Dashboard
items.text: dashboards/unifi-site-manager.json (Grafana, Prometheus data source, site variable): consoles and disconnected consoles, devices offline, firmware updates, clients, WAN ports down; average latency and packet loss by WAN interface, WAN port states, the internet connections with their ISP and expected speeds; clients and Wi-Fi retries by site, the devices offline, the consoles; the requests of Tapyr and the 429 responses of the API.

items.title: Known caveats
items.text:
• The statistics of the sites and the reportedState of the consoles vary with the UniFi Network and UniFi OS versions (as documented): every field is optional, and a missing one skips its sample.
  • pageSize counts consoles on /v1/devices (each with all its devices), not devices. No maximum page size is documented: the package asks for 100.
  • The ISP metrics of the dashboards read back 2 hours (last_over_time), since a window arrives 30 minutes after it ends.

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text:
Every field of every document kind of tapyr/v1alpha1, generated from the JSON Schemas that Tapyr validates configuration files with. The configuration model explains the kinds and shows examples. Editors validate and complete configuration files with the combined schema tapyr.json, for example with the YAML language server:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kentrow/tapyr/main/schemas/v1alpha1/tapyr.json

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The documents of a Tapyr configuration.

Kind Description Account An instance of a provider with credentials, params, targets and labels. Job What to collect for an account, from a template or inline. Output Where collected samples are sent. Settings Global settings (at most one document).

items.title: Provider packages
items.text:
The documents of a provider package (providers/<name>/).

Kind Description Provider An API family: base URL, auth, pagination, error semantics and rate limits. JobTemplate A reusable job definition shipped by a provider package. Simulation The simulator of a provider package (sim/sim.yaml). Scenario A simulator scenario of a provider package (sim/scenarios/*.yaml).

items.title: Command line
items.text: Every command and flag of tapyr: command line reference.

items.title: Account
items.text:
An instance of a provider with credentials, params, targets and labels.

Schema: account.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

Field Type Required Description apiVersion tapyr/v1alpha1 yes Version of the configuration format. kind Account yes Kind of the document. metadata ObjectMeta yes Name and description of the document. spec AccountSpec yes Specification of the document.

items.title: ObjectMeta
items.text:
ObjectMeta identifies a document.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Name yes Name of the document, unique per kind.

items.title: AccountSpec
items.text:
AccountSpec is the specification of an Account.

Field Type Required Description budget AccountBudget Budget share of this account. labels map of string to string Labels added to every sample from this account. Keys match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. params map of string to string Params declared by the provider. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. provider Name yes Provider instantiated by the account. secrets map of string to SecretRef Secrets declared by the provider, as references to environment variables or files. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. targets list of Target Targets of a multi-target account (for example one entry per device). Jobs run once per target. tls TLSClient tls settings for connections to the provider.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: AccountBudget
items.text:
AccountBudget configures the share of quotas the account may use.

Field Type Required Description scaleRates boolean scaleRates also scales rate and concurrency limits by the share. share number Share of every quota limit Tapyr may use, when other consumers share the same credentials. In (0, 1]. Default 1. Greater than 0. Maximum 1.

items.title: SecretRef
items.text:
A secret read from an environment variable ({env: NAME}) or a file ({file: /path}).

Field Type Required Description env string Name of an environment variable holding the secret. Minimum length 1. file string Path of a file holding the secret, relative to the declaring file. Minimum length 1.
  • Exactly one field is set.

items.title: Target
items.text:
Target is one endpoint of a multi-target account.

Field Type Required Description labels map of string to string Labels added to every sample from this target. Keys match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. name Name yes Name of the target, unique within the account. params map of string to string Params overriding the account params. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. secrets map of string to SecretRef Secrets overriding the account secrets. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.

items.title: TLSClient
items.text:
TLSClient configures TLS towards the provider.

Field Type Required Description caFile string caFile is a PEM bundle of trusted CAs, relative to the declaring file. insecureSkipVerify boolean insecureSkipVerify disables certificate verification. Logged loudly.

items.title: Command line
items.text:
Tapyr polls metric-oriented vendor APIs within their rate limits and exposes or pushes the collected data as Prometheus or OTLP metrics.

Every command reads the configuration from --config (files or directories, repeatable) or TAPYR_CONFIG.

items.title: Global flags
items.text: Flag Default Description --config string configuration file or directory, repeatable (env TAPYR_CONFIG) --log-format string log format: json, text (env TAPYR_LOG_FORMAT) --log-level string log level: debug, info, warn, error (env TAPYR_LOG_LEVEL)

items.title: tapyr plan
items.text:
Compute, offline, the effective interval of every job and the projected consumption of every quota scope over a full window. Estimates use the run history of the state store when it exists, else estimate.pagesPerRun. Exit code 3 when the plan is infeasible.

tapyr plan [flags]
Flag Default Description --fanout string fan-out hint: <parent>=<instances>, the parent as named in forEach (its template, or its job with forEach.job), repeatable --output string table output format: table or json --provider-path string directory of provider packages, repeatable, after the providerPaths of the configuration

items.title: tapyr provider lint
items.text:
Validate a provider package (or every package of a directory): schema, CEL compilation, dashboards, and the contract test of tests/contract.yaml, run once against the package simulator at a fixed simulated time. The samples must equal tests/expected.prom; --update rewrites it instead. --catalog also requires the catalog metadata: display name, categories, maintainers, tier, validation and the source of every limit.

tapyr provider lint <dir> [flags]
Flag Default Description --catalog also require the catalog metadata (ADR 0011) --update write tests/expected.prom instead of comparing

items.title: tapyr provider list
items.text:
List the built-in provider packages and, when a configuration is given, the packages of its providerPaths, in precedence order. --output json adds the catalog metadata, the templates and the limits of every package, and the catalog categories (the input of the provider catalog).

tapyr provider list [flags]
Flag Default Description --output string table output format: table or json

items.title: tapyr record
items.text:
Run every instance of the selected jobs once, through the budget engine, and write the responses, anonymized, into --out: one JSON file per page, index.yaml and report.txt (the replaced paths, never the values). Parents of the selected fan-out jobs run too. Review report.txt before committing anything.

tapyr record --job J [--job ...] --out DIR [--anonymize FILE] [flags]
Flag Default Description --anonymize string file of additional anonymization rules (replace, keep) --job string job to record, repeatable --out string directory receiving the recording --provider-path string directory of provider packages, repeatable, after the providerPaths of the configuration

items.title: tapyr run
items.text:
Load and compile the configuration, then collect: run every job at its interval through the budget engine and expose the samples on /metrics. SIGHUP reloads the configuration; SIGINT and SIGTERM shut down gracefully.

tapyr run

items.title: tapyr schema
items.text:
Print the JSON Schema accepting any document kind (tapyr.json), or the schema of one kind with --kind. With --out, write the schemas to a directory.

tapyr schema [flags]
Flag Default Description --kind string kind to print or write (Provider, JobTemplate, Account, Job, Output, Settings, Simulation, Scenario) --out string directory to write the schemas to

items.title: tapyr sim
items.text:
Serve the simulator of a provider package: its fixtures, with the auth, pagination and limits declared by the provider (429 with Retry-After and quota headers). --scenario overlays faults; --time-scale accelerates the simulated clock. --all serves every simulator from --listen-base, at the portOffset of its package (the next free offsets, in provider name order, for packages without one).

tapyr sim [flags]
Flag Default Description --all serve every simulator, at its port offset from --listen-base --listen string 127.0.0.1:8081 listen address --listen-base string 127.0.0.1:8081 address of the first simulator with --all --provider string provider package to simulate --provider-path string directory of user provider packages, repeatable --scenario string scenario of the package (sim/scenarios), for example quota-tight; with --all, applied to the simulators that have it --seed uint64 42 seed of the simulated randomness --time-scale float64 1 simulated time runs this many times faster than real time

items.title: tapyr validate
items.text:
Load the configuration, validate every document against its JSON Schema, check references and semantic rules, and report every error as file:line:column. Exit code 2 when the configuration is invalid.

tapyr validate [flags]
Flag Default Description --check-secrets also check that every referenced secret (environment variable or file) is set and not empty --provider-path string directory of provider packages, repeatable, after the providerPaths of the configuration

items.title: tapyr version
items.text:
Print the version, revision and Go version

tapyr version

items.title: Shell completion
items.text: tapyr completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell prints the completion script of a shell; tapyr completion <shell> --help explains how to load it.

items.title: Job
items.text:
What to collect for an account, from a template or inline.

Schema: job.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

Field Type Required Description apiVersion tapyr/v1alpha1 yes Version of the configuration format. kind Job yes Kind of the document. metadata ObjectMeta yes Name and description of the document. spec JobSpec yes Specification of the document.

items.title: ObjectMeta
items.text:
ObjectMeta identifies a document.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Name yes Name of the document, unique per kind.

items.title: JobSpec
items.text:
JobSpec is the specification of a Job.

Field Type Required Description account Name yes Account the job collects for. estimate Estimate Estimate gives hints to the planner before run history exists. extract Extract Extract maps responses to samples and inventory items. forEach ForEach forEach fans the job out over the inventory items of a parent. interval Duration Interval is the desired interval; the planner may stretch it. Defaults to the template's defaultInterval. labels map of string to string Labels added to every sample of the job. outputs list of Name Outputs receiving the job's samples. Default: all outputs. pagination Pagination Pagination overrides the provider default. priority Priority Priority of the job. Defaults to the template's defaultPriority, else normal. request Request Request to send. role JobRole Role of the job: inventory items, metrics, or both. staleAfter Duration staleAfter removes series of failing runs after this delay. Default: 3x the effective interval. template Name Template the job instantiates.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: Estimate
items.text:
Estimate gives hints to the planner.

Field Type Required Description pagesPerRun integer pagesPerRun is the expected number of pages per run. Minimum 1.

items.title: Extract
items.text:
Extract maps responses to samples and inventory items.

Field Type Required Description filter Expr Filter is a CEL expression on item; false skips the item. info list of InfoMetric Info metrics (value 1, descriptive labels) produced per item. inventory Inventory Inventory items produced per item (role inventory or both). items Expr Items is a CEL expression returning the list of items of a page. Default: response.body when it is a list. metrics list of Metric Metrics produced per item. partial boolean Partial emits the samples of a run even when a later page fails. post list of Metric Post metrics computed once per run over all pages (responses).

items.title: ForEach
items.text:
ForEach fans a job out over the inventory items of a parent job.

Field Type Required Description filter Expr Filter is a CEL expression on parent selecting a subset of items. job Name Job is the parent Job (same account), for inline jobs. maxInstances integer maxInstances caps the fan-out, against runaway discovery. Default 10000. Minimum 1. template Name Template is the parent JobTemplate, instantiated implicitly for the account when no job references it. vars map of string to Expr Vars maps request variables to CEL expressions on parent. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$. Examples 30s, 5m, 1h30m.

items.title: Pagination
items.text:
Pagination configures how successive pages are requested.

Field Type Required Description cursor CursorPagination Cursor pagination (type cursor). expression ExpressionPagination Expression pagination computed by CEL (type expression). linkHeader LinkHeaderPagination linkHeader pagination following RFC 8288 Link headers (type link_header). maxPages integer maxPages is a hard safety cap on pages per run. Default 100. Minimum 1. offset OffsetPagination Offset pagination (type offset). page PagePagination Page pagination (type page). type string yes Type of pagination. One of none, offset, page, link_header, cursor, expression.
  • When type is offset: offset is required.
  • When type is page: page is required.
  • When type is cursor: cursor is required.
  • When type is expression: expression is required.

items.title: Priority
items.text: Type: string. One of critical, high, normal, low.

items.title: Request
items.text:
Request describes the HTTP request of a job.

Field Type Required Description body map of string to Value Body is a JSON object for POST queries; values are literals, secrets or CEL expressions. headers map of string to string Headers merged over the provider defaults (the job wins). idempotent boolean Idempotent allows retrying POST requests. method string Method of the request. POST is allowed only for read-only queries. Default GET. One of GET, HEAD, POST. path string yes Path relative to the base URL, with {var} placeholders resolved from discovery variables, target params and account params. Pattern ^/. query map of string to Value Query parameters; values are literals, secrets or CEL expressions. readOnly boolean readOnly must be true for POST requests: Tapyr never writes to providers. timeout Duration Timeout of a single request. Defaults to the provider default.

items.title: JobRole
items.text: Type: string. Default metrics. One of inventory, metrics, both.

items.title: Expr
items.text:
CEL expression.

Type: string. Minimum length 1.

items.title: InfoMetric
items.text:
InfoMetric produces an _info metric: value 1 and descriptive labels.

Field Type Required Description help string Help text of the metric. labels map of string to Expr yes Labels maps label names to CEL expressions returning strings. Keys match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. name string yes Name of the metric, ending with _info. Pattern ^[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*_info$. skipIf Expr skipIf is a CEL expression; true skips the sample.

items.title: Inventory
items.text:
Inventory produces inventory items for child jobs.

Field Type Required Description fields map of string to Expr Fields maps field names to CEL expressions, available as parent.<field>. Keys match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. key Expr yes Key is a CEL expression returning the unique key of an item. ttl Duration ttl of cached items. Default: 3x the job's effective interval.

items.title: Metric
items.text:
Metric maps items to samples of one metric.

Field Type Required Description accumulate boolean Accumulate sums successive window values into a persisted counter (type counter only). help string Help text of the metric. labels map of string to Expr Labels maps label names to CEL expressions returning strings. Keys match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. name string yes Name of the metric (Prometheus naming rules). Pattern ^[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*$. skipIf Expr skipIf is a CEL expression; true skips the sample. timestamp Expr Timestamp is a CEL expression returning the source timestamp. type string Type of the metric. Default gauge. One of gauge, counter. unit string Unit of the metric, preferably a Prometheus base unit. value Expr yes Value is a CEL expression returning a number or a bool. windowField Expr windowField is a CEL expression identifying the window of a value, used by accumulate to avoid counting a window twice.

items.title: CursorPagination
items.text:
CursorPagination passes a cursor extracted from each response.

Field Type Required Description cursor Expr yes Cursor is a CEL expression extracting the next cursor; empty or null stops. header string Header carrying the cursor, instead of a query parameter. pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. pageSizeParam string pageSizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. param string Param is the query parameter carrying the cursor.

items.title: ExpressionPagination
items.text:
ExpressionPagination computes the next request with CEL.

Field Type Required Description next Expr yes Next is a CEL expression returning {query: {...}} for the next page, or null.

items.title: LinkHeaderPagination
items.text:
LinkHeaderPagination follows RFC 8288 Link headers.

Field Type Required Description pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. pageSizeParam string pageSizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. rel string Rel is the link relation of the next page. Default next.

items.title: OffsetPagination
items.text:

Field Type Required Description limitParam string yes limitParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. Minimum length 1. offsetParam string yes offsetParam is the query parameter carrying the offset. Minimum length 1. pageSize integer yes pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. start integer Start is the first offset. Default 0. Minimum 0. stop Expr Stop is a CEL expression; pagination stops when it returns true. total Expr Total is a CEL expression returning the total number of items.

items.title: PagePagination

PagePagination requests pages by page number.

Field Type Required Description pageParam string yes pageParam is the query parameter carrying the page number. Minimum length 1. pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. sizeParam string sizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. start integer Start is the first page number. Default 1. Minimum 0. stop Expr Stop is a CEL expression; pagination stops when it returns true. total Expr Total is a CEL expression returning the total number of items.

A literal string, {secret: name} or {expr: cel}.

Either a string, or an object:

Field Type Required Description expr string CEL expression evaluated at runtime. Minimum length 1. secret string Name of a secret declared by the provider and supplied by the account. Pattern ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.

items.title: Output
items.text:

Schema: output.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

items.title: OutputSpec
items.text:
OutputSpec is the specification of an Output.

Field Type Required Description externalLabels map of string to string externalLabels added to every sample sent through this output. Keys match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. otlp OTLPOutput otlp pushes OTLP metrics (type otlp). processing list of ProcessingRule Processing is an ordered list of rules applied to the samples of the jobs sent to this output only, with the semantics of Prometheus metric_relabel_configs (ADR 0012). Self-metrics are never processed. prometheus PrometheusOutput Prometheus pull exposition on /metrics (type prometheus, at most one). queue Queue Queue of a push output (not allowed for prometheus). remoteWrite RemoteWriteOutput remoteWrite pushes with Prometheus remote write 1.0 (type remote_write). type string yes Type of output. Format uri. headers map of string to StringOrSecret Headers added to every request; values are literals or secrets. protocol string Protocol: http/protobuf or grpc. Default http/protobuf. One of keep, drop, labelkeep, labeldrop. regex string Regex is an RE2 regular expression, fully anchored. keep and drop default to (.*); labelkeep and labeldrop require it. separator string Separator joins the values of sourceLabels (keep and drop). Default ;. sourceLabels list of string sourceLabels are the labels whose values are joined and matched (keep and drop, required); __name__ is the metric name, a missing label the empty string. Each item: pattern ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$.
