items.text:
ProviderMeta identifies a provider package.

Field Type Required Description categories list of Name Categories of the provider, from providers/categories.yaml, the main one first. Unique items. description string Description is free text for humans. displayName string displayName is the name of the provider in the catalog, for example "Cisco Meraki Dashboard". Like categories, maintainers, tier and validation, it is optional, and required by tapyr provider lint --catalog (ADR 0011). docs string Docs links to the vendor API documentation. Format uri. maintainers list of string Maintainers are the GitHub handles, without @, of the people who answer for the package. Unique items. Each item: pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?$. name Name yes Name of the provider, unique across built-in and user packages. tier string Tier says who maintains the package: official (the Tapyr maintainers) or community (the maintainers listed). One of official, community. validation Validation Validation says how the package was last tested. version string yes Version of the provider package (semver). Breaking changes to metric names or labels bump the major version. Pattern ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$.

items.title: ProviderSpec
items.text:
ProviderSpec is the specification of a Provider.

Field Type Required Description auth Auth Auth applied to every request. Defaults to type none. baseURL Template yes baseURL of the API. Template evaluated per account and target, for example {{ .params.baseURL | default "https://api.example.com/v1" }}. defaults RequestDefaults Defaults applied to every request. errors ErrorSemantics Errors declares how the API signals rate limiting, authentication failures and retryable errors. limits list of Limit Limits declares every rate limit, concurrency limit and quota of the API. pagination Pagination Pagination used by job templates that do not override it. params list of ParamSpec Params an Account may or must provide. redirects Redirects Redirects lists the other hosts a response may redirect requests to. Redirects to another host are not followed otherwise: credentials only go to the base URL and to these hosts. secrets list of ParamSpec Secrets an Account may or must provide.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Validation records the last validation of a provider package.

Field Type Required Description date string Date of the validation, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM. Required by tapyr provider lint --catalog with status real-platform. Pattern ^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(-(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01]))?$. notes string Notes is free text: what was covered, what the package was built from. platformVersion string platformVersion is the version of the API, platform or firmware validated against, for example "RutOS 07.24.5". Required by tapyr provider lint --catalog with status real-platform. status string yes Status is simulator (tested against its simulator only) or real-platform (run against the real API). One of simulator, real-platform.

items.title: Auth
items.text:
Auth configures authentication.

Field Type Required Description basic BasicAuth Basic sends HTTP basic credentials (type basic). bearer BearerAuth Bearer sends Authorization: Bearer <token> (type bearer). header HeaderAuth Header sends a static value in a header (type header). oauth2ClientCredentials OAuth2ClientCredentials oauth2ClientCredentials obtains tokens with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant (type oauth2_client_credentials). plugin PluginAuth Plugin delegates to a Go auth plugin (type plugin). sessionLogin SessionLogin sessionLogin posts credentials to obtain a session token (type session_login). type string yes Type of authentication. One of none, header, bearer, basic, oauth2_client_credentials, session_login, plugin.
  • When type is basic: basic is required.
  • When type is bearer: bearer is required.
  • When type is header: header is required.
  • When type is oauth2_client_credentials: oauth2ClientCredentials is required.
  • When type is plugin: plugin is required.
  • When type is session_login: sessionLogin is required.

items.title: Template
items.text:
Go text/template evaluated per account and target.

Type: string.

items.title: RequestDefaults
items.text:
RequestDefaults are applied to every request of the provider.

Field Type Required Description headers map of string to Template Headers added to every request. Values are templates. timeout Duration Timeout of a single request. Defaults to settings.collection.defaultTimeout.

items.title: ErrorSemantics
items.text:
ErrorSemantics declares how the provider signals errors.

Field Type Required Description authFailed StatusMatcher authFailed matches authentication failures (default 401). rateLimited RateLimitedErrors rateLimited matches rate-limited responses. retryable StatusMatcher Retryable matches transient errors (default 500, 502, 503, 504).

items.title: Limit
items.text:
Limit is a constraint of the provider API, enforced by the budget engine for every request (see docs/spec/04-budget-engine.md).

Field Type Required Description appliesTo AppliesTo appliesTo restricts the requests the limit counts. burst integer Burst is the bucket capacity of a rate limit. Defaults to the rate per second, minimum 1. Minimum 1. description string Description is free text for humans, ideally with the source of the limit. initialMax integer initialMax is the conservative quota maximum used with max: auto until the first limit header is observed. Minimum 1. kind string yes Kind of limit: rate (token bucket), concurrency or quota (window). One of rate, concurrency, quota. max IntOrAuto Max is the maximum of a concurrency limit, or of a quota per window. A quota may use "auto" to learn it from response headers. name Name yes Name of the limit, unique within the provider. rate Rate Rate is the refill rate of a rate limit, for example 10/s. scope Scope Scope partitions the limit (one counter per scope key). source LimitSource Source of the limit. Optional, and required on every limit by tapyr provider lint --catalog. sync QuotaSync Sync reads quota state from response headers. window Window Window of a quota: a calendar period or a rolling duration.
  • When kind is rate: rate is required.
  • When kind is concurrency: max is required.
  • When kind is quota: max and window are required.

items.title: Pagination
items.text:
Pagination configures how successive pages are requested.

Field Type Required Description cursor CursorPagination Cursor pagination (type cursor). expression ExpressionPagination Expression pagination computed by CEL (type expression). linkHeader LinkHeaderPagination linkHeader pagination following RFC 8288 Link headers (type link_header). maxPages integer maxPages is a hard safety cap on pages per run. Default 100. Minimum 1. offset OffsetPagination Offset pagination (type offset). page PagePagination Page pagination (type page). type string yes Type of pagination. One of none, offset, page, link_header, cursor, expression.
  • When type is offset: offset is required.
  • When type is page: page is required.
  • When type is cursor: cursor is required.
  • When type is expression: expression is required.

items.title: ParamSpec
items.text:
ParamSpec declares a param or a secret that accounts provide.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Identifier yes Name of the param or secret. required boolean Required makes the param or secret mandatory for every account (or every target of a multi-target account).

items.title: Redirects
items.text:
Redirects allows HTTP redirects to other hosts.

Field Type Required Description hosts list of string yes Hosts the requests may be redirected to: a host name, or "*." and a domain for every host under it (for example "*.meraki.com"). Minimum items 1.

items.title: BasicAuth
items.text:
BasicAuth sends HTTP basic credentials.

Field Type Required Description password Value yes Password, usually {secret: name}. username Value yes Username, a literal or {secret: name}.

items.title: BearerAuth
items.text:
BearerAuth sends Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Field Type Required Description token Value yes Token, usually {secret: name}.

items.title: HeaderAuth
items.text:
HeaderAuth sends a static credential in a request header.

Field Type Required Description format string Format of the header value; {value} is replaced by the value, for example "Token {value}". Default {value}. name string yes Name of the header, for example X-API-Key. Minimum length 1. value Value yes Value of the header, usually {secret: name}.

items.title: OAuth2ClientCredentials
items.text:
OAuth2ClientCredentials configures the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant.

Field Type Required Description audience string Audience requested, when the server requires one. authStyle string authStyle sends the client credentials in the Authorization header or in the request body. Default header. One of header, body. clientId Value yes ClientID, a literal or {secret: name}. clientSecret Value yes ClientSecret, usually {secret: name}. extraParams map of string to string extraParams added to the token request. scopes list of string Scopes requested. tokenURL Template yes tokenURL of the authorization server. Template.

items.title: PluginAuth
items.text:
PluginAuth selects a Go auth plugin, for flows that cannot be expressed declaratively.

Field Type Required Description config object Config is passed to the plugin, which validates it. name string yes Name of the plugin, as registered in internal/auth/plugins. Pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.

items.title: SessionLogin
items.text:
SessionLogin posts credentials to a login endpoint and applies the returned token to subsequent requests.

Field Type Required Description apply TokenApply yes Apply describes how the token is attached to requests. expiresIn Expr expiresIn is a CEL expression returning the token lifetime as a duration. logout LogoutRequest Logout closes a session when its token is replaced and when Tapyr stops, for APIs that keep sessions open until they are closed. perTarget boolean perTarget keeps one session per target of a multi-target account. refreshBefore Duration refreshBefore renews the session this long before it expires. Default 30s. request LoginRequest yes Request is the login request. token Expr yes Token is a CEL expression extracting the token from the login response.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$. Examples 30s, 5m, 1h30m.

items.title: StatusMatcher
items.text:
StatusMatcher matches responses by HTTP status code.

Field Type Required Description statuses list of integer Statuses that match. Minimum items 1. Each item: minimum 100, maximum 599.

items.title: RateLimitedErrors
items.text:
RateLimitedErrors matches rate-limited responses and configures penalties.

Field Type Required Description defaultPenalty Duration defaultPenalty applies when no Retry-After header is present. It grows exponentially on consecutive rate-limited responses, up to 10 minutes. Default 2s. penalize string Penalize the narrowest applicable scope, or all applicable scopes. Default narrowest. One of narrowest, all. retryAfterHeader string retryAfterHeader carries the penalty in seconds or as an HTTP date. Default Retry-After. statuses list of integer Statuses that signal rate limiting (default 429). Minimum items 1. Each item: minimum 100, maximum 599.

items.title: AppliesTo
items.text:
AppliesTo restricts the requests a limit counts.

Field Type Required Description authRequests string authRequests selects regular requests and token requests: include (both), only (token requests only) or exclude (regular requests only). Default include. One of include, only, exclude. endpoints list of string Endpoints are globs on the templated path: * matches within one segment, ** matches any number of segments. Each item: pattern ^/. methods list of string Methods the limit counts. Each item: one of GET, HEAD, POST. requestsWithVar Identifier requestsWithVar counts only requests where this variable is set.

items.title: IntOrAuto
items.text: Type: integer or string. Pattern ^auto$. Minimum 1.

items.title: Rate
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?/(s|m|h)$. Examples 10/s, 600/m.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Scope partitions a limit.

Field Type Required Description by list of string By lists the scope dimensions: instance, provider, account, target, credential, endpoint or var:<name>. Empty means instance. Unique items. Each item: pattern ^(instance|provider|account|target|credential|endpoint|var:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$.

items.title: LimitSource
items.text:
LimitSource says where a limit comes from.

Field Type Required Description date string Date the source was checked or the measurement made, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM. Pattern ^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(-(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01]))?$. kind string yes Kind is vendor-docs (the vendor documentation, with its url), measured (against the real API, with its date) or assumed (nothing documented). One of vendor-docs, measured, assumed. url string url of the vendor documentation, or of the notes of a measurement. Format uri.

items.title: QuotaSync
items.text:
QuotaSync names the response headers carrying quota state.

Field Type Required Description limitHeader string limitHeader carries the quota maximum. remainingHeader string remainingHeader carries the remaining quota. resetHeader string resetHeader carries the reset time (epoch seconds or delta seconds).

items.title: Window
items.text:
Window is the window of a quota: exactly one of period or rolling.

Field Type Required Description monthDay integer monthDay is the day of month windows reset (1 to 31; the last day of shorter months). Default 1. Minimum 1. Maximum 31. period string Period of a fixed calendar window. One of minute, hour, day, week, month. resetAt string resetAt is the time of day (HH:MM, 24h) at which day, week and month windows reset. Default 00:00. Pattern ^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$. rolling Duration Rolling is the duration of a rolling window (1-minute precision). timezone string Timezone of the calendar (IANA name). Default UTC. weekStart string weekStart is the first day of week windows. Default monday. One of monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday.

items.title: CursorPagination
items.text:
CursorPagination passes a cursor extracted from each response.

Field Type Required Description cursor Expr yes Cursor is a CEL expression extracting the next cursor; empty or null stops. header string Header carrying the cursor, instead of a query parameter. pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. pageSizeParam string pageSizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. param string Param is the query parameter carrying the cursor.

items.title: ExpressionPagination
items.text:
ExpressionPagination computes the next request with CEL.

Field Type Required Description next Expr yes Next is a CEL expression returning {query: {...}} for the next page, or null.

items.title: LinkHeaderPagination
items.text:
LinkHeaderPagination follows RFC 8288 Link headers.

Field Type Required Description pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. pageSizeParam string pageSizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. rel string Rel is the link relation of the next page. Default next.

items.title: OffsetPagination
items.text:
OffsetPagination requests pages by item offset.

Field Type Required Description limitParam string yes limitParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. Minimum length 1. offsetParam string yes offsetParam is the query parameter carrying the offset. Minimum length 1. pageSize integer yes pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. start integer Start is the first offset. Default 0. Minimum 0. stop Expr Stop is a CEL expression; pagination stops when it returns true. total Expr Total is a CEL expression returning the total number of items.

items.title: PagePagination
items.text:
PagePagination requests pages by page number.

Field Type Required Description pageParam string yes pageParam is the query parameter carrying the page number. Minimum length 1. pageSize integer pageSize is the number of items per page. Minimum 1. sizeParam string sizeParam is the query parameter carrying the page size. start integer Start is the first page number. Default 1. Minimum 0. stop Expr Stop is a CEL expression; pagination stops when it returns true. total Expr Total is a CEL expression returning the total number of items.

items.title: Identifier
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.

items.title: Value
items.text:
A literal string, {secret: name} or {expr: cel}.

Either a string, or an object:

Field Type Required Description expr string CEL expression evaluated at runtime. Minimum length 1. secret string Name of a secret declared by the provider and supplied by the account. Pattern ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.
  • Exactly one field is set.

items.title: TokenApply
items.text:
TokenApply attaches a session token to requests, as a header or a cookie.

Field Type Required Description cookie string Cookie that carries the token. format string Format of the header value; {token} is replaced by the token. Default {token}. header string Header that carries the token.

items.title: Expr
items.text:
CEL expression.

Type: string. Minimum length 1.

items.title: LogoutRequest
items.text:
LogoutRequest is the request that closes a session, sent with the token applied.

Field Type Required Description method string Method of the logout request. Default POST. One of POST, GET, DELETE. path string yes Path of the logout endpoint, relative to the base URL. Pattern ^/.

items.title: LoginRequest
items.text:
LoginRequest is the request that opens a session.

Field Type Required Description body map of string to Value Body is a JSON object; values are literals, secrets or CEL expressions. headers map of string to string Headers added to the login request. method string Method of the login request. Default POST. One of POST, GET. path string yes Path of the login endpoint, relative to the base URL. Pattern ^/.

items.title: Scenario
items.text:
A simulator scenario of a provider package (sim/scenarios/*.yaml).

Schema: scenario.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

Field Type Required Description apiVersion tapyr/v1alpha1 yes Version of the configuration format. kind Scenario yes Kind of the document. metadata ObjectMeta yes Name and description of the document. spec ScenarioSpec yes Specification of the document.

items.title: ObjectMeta
items.text:
ObjectMeta identifies a document.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Name yes Name of the document, unique per kind.

items.title: ScenarioSpec
items.text:
ScenarioSpec is the specification of a Scenario.

Field Type Required Description steps list of ScenarioStep Steps of the timeline.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: ScenarioStep
items.text:
ScenarioStep applies from at until at + for (or until the end), in simulated time since the simulator start.

Field Type Required Description at Duration At is the start of the step. errors ScenarioErrors Errors answers a ratio of the requests to matching routes with a status. externalConsumption ExternalConsumption externalConsumption simulates another client consuming a quota. fixtures map of string to string Fixtures replaces the fixture of routes, by route path, to simulate inventory changes. Files are relative to the sim/ directory and take the {var} placeholders of the route. for Duration For is the duration of the step; empty means until the end. latency ScenarioLatency Latency delays the responses (log-normal, in simulated time). limits map of string to ScenarioLimit Limits overrides the max of named quota limits. outage boolean Outage closes connections without a response. tokenExpiry boolean tokenExpiry invalidates, when the step starts, the tokens issued before it.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$. Examples 30s, 5m, 1h30m.

items.title: ScenarioErrors
items.text:
ScenarioErrors injects error responses.

Field Type Required Description ratio number yes Ratio of the matching requests that fail (0 to 1). Minimum 0. Maximum 1. routes list of string Routes are globs on the route paths (* within a segment, ** across segments). Empty means every route. status integer yes Status of the injected responses. Minimum 400. Maximum 599.

items.title: ExternalConsumption
items.text:
ExternalConsumption consumes a quota at a steady rate.

Field Type Required Description limit Name yes Limit is the name of a quota limit of the provider. ratePerHour number yes ratePerHour is the consumption rate. Minimum 0.

items.title: ScenarioLatency
items.text:
ScenarioLatency is a log-normal response delay given by two quantiles.

Field Type Required Description p50 Duration yes P50 is the median delay. p99 Duration P99 is the 99th percentile, at least P50.

items.title: ScenarioLimit
items.text:
ScenarioLimit overrides a quota limit.

Field Type Required Description max integer yes Max of the quota per window. Minimum 0.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Global settings (at most one document).

Schema: settings.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

Field Type Required Description apiVersion tapyr/v1alpha1 yes Version of the configuration format. kind Settings yes Kind of the document. metadata ObjectMeta yes Name and description of the document. spec SettingsSpec yes Specification of the document.

items.title: ObjectMeta
items.text:
ObjectMeta identifies a document.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Name yes Name of the document, unique per kind.

items.title: SettingsSpec
items.text:
SettingsSpec is the specification of Settings.

Field Type Required Description budget BudgetSettings Budget configures the budget engine and the planner. circuitBreaker CircuitBreakerSettings circuitBreaker configures the per-account circuit breakers. collection CollectionSettings Collection configures request execution. log LogSettings Log configures logging. Flags and environment variables win. mapping MappingSettings Mapping configures CEL evaluation limits. providerPaths list of string providerPaths lists directories of user provider packages, in addition to the built-in packages. retry RetrySettings Retry configures retries of transient errors. selfMetrics SelfMetricsSettings selfMetrics configures Tapyr's own metrics. server ServerSettings Server is the HTTP server (metrics, health, status API, UI). state StateSettings State is the persistent state store.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: BudgetSettings
items.text:
BudgetSettings configures the budget engine and the planner.

Field Type Required Description maxStretch number maxStretch caps the interval stretch factor applied to a priority class before the planner moves to the next class. Default 12. Minimum 1. replanInterval Duration replanInterval is the period of mid-window replanning. Default 15m. replanOnProjection boolean replanOnProjection replans at once when the consumption projected by the current plan until the end of a quota window exceeds its remaining budget, for example when another client starts spending the same quota, instead of waiting for the next replanInterval. Default true. retryReserve Percent retryReserve is the share of every quota reserved for retries, from 0% to 50%. Default 10%.

items.title: CircuitBreakerSettings
items.text:
CircuitBreakerSettings configures the per-account circuit breakers.

Field Type Required Description cooldown Duration Cooldown before the half-open probe. Default 2m. failureThreshold integer failureThreshold is the number of consecutive transient failures that opens the circuit. Default 5. Minimum 1. maxCooldown Duration maxCooldown caps the cooldown, which doubles on repeated openings. Default 30m.

items.title: CollectionSettings
items.text:
CollectionSettings configures request execution.

Field Type Required Description defaultTimeout Duration defaultTimeout of a request when the provider sets none. Default 30s. jitter Percent Jitter spreads scheduled runs, from 0% to 50% of the interval. Default 10%. maxConcurrentRequests integer maxConcurrentRequests bounds in-flight requests across all providers. Default 32. Minimum 1.

items.title: LogSettings
items.text:
LogSettings configures logging.

Field Type Required Description format string Format: json or text. Default json. One of json, text. level string Level: debug, info, warn or error. Default info. One of debug, info, warn, error.

items.title: MappingSettings
items.text:
MappingSettings configures CEL evaluation limits.

Field Type Required Description labelConflict string labelConflict resolves labels set both by the mapping and by account, target or job labels: override (job > target > account > mapping) or error. Default override. One of override, error. maxCost integer maxCost is the CEL cost limit per expression evaluation. Default 1000000. Minimum 1. maxItemsPerRun integer maxItemsPerRun caps the items extracted by a run. Default 100000. Minimum 1. maxSamplesPerRun integer maxSamplesPerRun caps the samples produced by a run. Default 200000. Minimum 1.

items.title: RetrySettings
items.text:
RetrySettings configures retries with exponential backoff and full jitter.

Field Type Required Description initialBackoff Duration initialBackoff before the first retry. Default 1s. maxAttempts integer maxAttempts per request, including the first attempt. Default 4. Minimum 1. maxBackoff Duration maxBackoff caps the backoff. Default 60s. multiplier number Multiplier of the backoff between attempts. Default 2. Minimum 1.

items.title: SelfMetricsSettings
items.text:
SelfMetricsSettings configures Tapyr's own metrics.

Field Type Required Description interval Duration Interval between two pushes of the self-metrics to Outputs. Default 30s. outputs list of Name Outputs that also receive the self-metrics (always served on /metrics/self).

items.title: ServerSettings
items.text:
ServerSettings configures the HTTP server.

Field Type Required Description basicAuth ServerBasicAuth basicAuth protects /api and /ui. debug DebugSettings Debug is the live debug endpoint exposing raw responses. listen string Listen address. Default 127.0.0.1:9790. tls ServerTLS tls serves HTTPS with the given certificate. A reverse proxy is the recommended way to terminate TLS. ui UISettings ui is the embedded read-only web UI.

items.title: StateSettings
items.text:
StateSettings configures the state store.

Field Type Required Description path string Path of the SQLite database, relative to the declaring file. The built-in default is relative to the working directory. Default ./data/tapyr.db.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$. Examples 30s, 5m, 1h30m.

items.title: Percent
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%$. Examples 10%.

items.title: ServerBasicAuth
items.text:
ServerBasicAuth protects the server with HTTP basic authentication.

Field Type Required Description password SecretRef yes Password secret. protectMetrics boolean protectMetrics also protects /metrics and /metrics/self. username SecretRef yes Username secret.

items.title: DebugSettings
items.text:
DebugSettings configures the live debug endpoint.

Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Enabled exposes the last raw responses (redacted) in the status API. maxBodyBytes integer maxBodyBytes truncates the raw responses kept for debugging. Default 1048576. Minimum 1.

items.title: ServerTLS
items.text:
ServerTLS holds the server certificate files, relative to the declaring file.

Field Type Required Description certFile string yes certFile is the PEM certificate chain. Minimum length 1. keyFile string yes keyFile is the PEM private key. Minimum length 1.

items.title: UISettings
items.text:
UISettings configures the web UI.

Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Enabled serves the UI under /ui/. Default true.

items.title: SecretRef
items.text:
A secret read from an environment variable ({env: NAME}) or a file ({file: /path}).

Field Type Required Description env string Name of an environment variable holding the secret. Minimum length 1. file string Path of a file holding the secret, relative to the declaring file. Minimum length 1.
  • Exactly one field is set.

items.title: Simulation
items.text:
The simulator of a provider package (sim/sim.yaml).

Schema: simulation.json. Explanations and examples: configuration model.

Field Type Required Description apiVersion tapyr/v1alpha1 yes Version of the configuration format. kind Simulation yes Kind of the document. metadata ObjectMeta yes Name and description of the document. spec SimulationSpec yes Specification of the document.

items.title: ObjectMeta
items.text:
ObjectMeta identifies a document.

Field Type Required Description description string Description is free text for humans. name Name yes Name of the document, unique per kind.

items.title: SimulationSpec
items.text:
SimulationSpec is the specification of a Simulation.

Field Type Required Description auth SimulationAuth Auth lists the credentials the simulator accepts. The way they are checked follows the provider auth type. basePath string basePath is the path prefix of the API (the path part of the provider base URL). Routes are relative to it. Default /. Pattern ^/. headers map of string to string Headers added to every response, computed from the limit state: "limit:<name>.max", "limit:<name>.remaining" or "limit:<name>.reset" (seconds until the window resets). inventory SimulationInventory Inventory generates synthetic items for templated fixtures. portOffset integer portOffset is the port of the simulator in tapyr sim --all, as an offset from --listen-base, so that adding a package does not move the others. Simulators without one take the ports after the largest declared offset, in provider name order. Minimum 0. routes list of SimulationRoute yes Routes served by the simulator. Unknown routes return 404. Minimum items 1.

items.title: Name
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.

items.title: SimulationAuth
items.text:
SimulationAuth configures the credentials accepted by the simulator.

Field Type Required Description accept SimulationCredentials Accept lists the accepted credentials. They are fake values by design. loginResponse string loginResponse is a JSON fixture answered by the login endpoint, relative to the sim/ directory; {token} and {expiresIn} (seconds) are replaced. Default: {"token": "{token}", "expiresIn": {expiresIn}}. tokenLifetime Duration tokenLifetime of the tokens issued by the token and login endpoints, in simulated time. Default 10m.

items.title: SimulationInventory
items.text:
SimulationInventory is a synthetic inventory: sets of items, each item under a parent item of another set.

Field Type Required Description seed integer Seed of the generated values. The same seed gives the same items and the same dynamics. Default 42. sets list of SimulationSet yes Sets of items, generated in order: a parent set comes first. Minimum items 1.

items.title: SimulationRoute
items.text:
SimulationRoute is an endpoint of the simulator.

Field Type Required Description method string Method of the route. Default GET. One of GET, HEAD, POST. pagination string Pagination serves the fixture items page by page. Its parameters come from the job templates requesting this path, or from the provider. Default none. One of none, offset, page, link_header, cursor, expression. path string yes Path of the route, relative to basePath, with {var} segments. Pattern ^/. response SimulationResponse yes Response returned by the route.

items.title: SimulationCredentials
items.text:
SimulationCredentials are accepted credentials per auth type.

Field Type Required Description basic list of SimulationBasicCredential Basic credentials accepted with auth type basic. bearer list of string Bearer tokens accepted with auth type bearer. clients list of SimulationClient Clients accepted by the token endpoint with auth type oauth2_client_credentials. header list of string Header values accepted with auth type header, before the format of the provider auth is applied. logins list of SimulationBasicCredential Logins accepted by the login endpoint with auth type session_login: the login body must carry both values. plugin object Plugin holds the credentials accepted by the simulator side of an auth plugin (type plugin), read by the plugin.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Type: string. Pattern ^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$. Examples 30s, 5m, 1h30m.

items.title: SimulationSet
items.text:
SimulationSet is a set of generated items.

Field Type Required Description count integer yes Count of items (per parent item when Parent is set). Minimum 0. Maximum 100000. name Name yes Name of the set, used by the template helpers. parent Name Parent set: count items are generated under each of its items.

items.title: SimulationResponse
items.text:
SimulationResponse is the response of a route.

Field Type Required Description file string File is the JSON fixture, relative to the sim/ directory. {var} placeholders are replaced by the route variables. Paginated routes need a JSON array, or a list at ItemsField. Minimum length 1. headers map of string to string Headers added to the response. itemsField string itemsField is the dotted path of the list a paginated route serves page by page, inside an envelope; empty for a top-level array. status integer Status code of the response. Default 200. Minimum 100. Maximum 599. template string Template is a Go text/template fixture rendering JSON, relative to the sim/ directory (see docs/spec/08-simulator.md for its data and helpers). Exactly one of file and template is set. Minimum length 1.
  • Exactly one of file, template is set.

items.title: SimulationBasicCredential
items.text:
SimulationBasicCredential is a username and password pair.

Field Type Required Description password string yes Password accepted. username string yes Username accepted.

items.title: SimulationClient
items.text:
SimulationClient is an OAuth 2.0 client.

Field Type Required Description clientId string yes clientId accepted. clientSecret string yes clientSecret accepted.

items.title: Problem
items.text:
Many platforms are now cloud-managed and expose their telemetry only through REST APIs: network equipment first (Aruba Central, Cisco Meraki, Teltonika RMS, and many others), but also security services, Internet measurement, cloud costs, developer platforms and energy. Getting that telemetry into an open observability stack (Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, Mimir, any OTLP backend) is surprisingly painful:

  • Vertical exporters exist for some vendors (one project per vendor, hardcoded endpoints, inconsistent quality). Many vendors have none.
  • Generic tools (Telegraf inputs.http, Redpanda Connect, Vector) can call HTTP APIs, but treat rate limits as an afterthought: at best a per-input interval or a simple token bucket. None of them understands a daily or monthly quota, a limit scoped per organization, a quota shared with other consumers, or the need to plan polling to fit a budget.
  • Quota exhaustion is a silent failure. When a daily quota runs out at 3 pm, every device polled through that API "goes dark" until midnight UTC, and the root cause sits two layers below the symptom.

items.title: Vision
items.text:
Tapyr is a declarative API-to-metrics gateway where:

  1. A provider (an API family, e.g. "Meraki Dashboard API v1") is described once, declaratively: base URL, auth, pagination, error semantics, and all of its rate limits.
  2. Accounts instantiate a provider with credentials (one Meraki API key, one Aruba Central tenant, one Teltonika router).
  3. Jobs describe what to collect: an endpoint, a desired interval, a priority, optional discovery fan-out, and a CEL mapping from JSON to metrics.
  4. A budget engine guarantees that every limit is respected, plans effective intervals to fit quotas, keeps a reserve for retries, and syncs with the quota headers returned by the API.
  5. Collected data is exposed or pushed in standard formats: Prometheus exposition (pull), Prometheus remote write (push, covers Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, Mimir, Thanos), OTLP (push).
  6. Tapyr observes itself and exposes rich self-metrics.
  7. Every provider ships with a simulator driven by the same definition, enforcing the same limits, so that providers can be developed and tested without access to the vendor platform.

Network first, not network only. Networks are the first use case: the built-in packages, the examples and the documentation start there. The core makes no network-specific assumption, and any metric-oriented API must be expressible as a provider package; a mechanism another domain needs is added to the engine as a generic feature (ADR 0011).

Long-term, provider packages (definition + default jobs + simulator fixtures + dashboards + tests) become a community ecosystem, in the spirit of Terraform providers or snmp_exporter modules, but declarative and therefore accessible to engineers who do not write Go. It grows in phases: first a static catalog on tapyr.eu generated from the packages of this repository, with catalog metadata on every package (who maintains it, how it was validated, the source of every limit); later, if justified, packages distributed as OCI artifacts.

items.title: Positioning
items.text: Tapyr is Tapyr is not A specialized gateway from REST APIs to metrics A general-purpose ETL or stream processor Declarative (YAML + CEL) A collection of hardcoded vendor exporters Read-only towards providers A configuration or automation tool A single static binary A platform requiring a database server

items.title: Target users
items.text:
• Network and infrastructure engineers who manage cloud-managed equipment and run an open observability stack (the first use case).
  • Engineers who monitor any other platform through a metric-oriented API with scarce quotas: security, energy, cloud costs, developer tools.
  • Observability consultants who need to integrate many vendor APIs quickly and must size API consumption upfront.
  • Contributors who know a vendor API well and want to package it for others.

items.title: Scope of v0.1.0
items.text:
Functional:

  • Declarative config model: Provider, Account, Job, Output (+ Settings), YAML, multi-document, splittable across files, validated by JSON Schema.
  • Budget engine: rate (token bucket), concurrency, fixed-window quotas (minute, hour, day, week, month, with reset time and timezone), rolling-window quotas; scopes (instance, account, target, credential, endpoint, request variables); header sync; 429 and Retry-After handling; retry reserve; priority-aware planning; persistent ledger.
  • tapyr plan: offline estimation of call consumption per quota and effective intervals.
  • tapyr validate: config and provider validation, including CEL type-checking.
  • Collection: auth types none, header, bearer, basic, oauth2_client_credentials, session_login (generic login flow), plus the aruba_central_classic auth plugin (rotating refresh tokens).
  • Pagination: none, offset, page, link_header, cursor, expression.
  • Discovery: jobs that fan out from the results of a parent job, with an inventory cache.
  • Multi-target accounts (one account, N device endpoints, e.g. Teltonika RutOS routers).
  • Retries with error classification, exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breaker per account.
  • CEL mapping: gauges, counters, _info metrics, labels, optional source timestamps.
  • Series lifecycle: staleness when a series disappears, deduplication of overlapping windows.
  • Outputs: Prometheus pull endpoint, Prometheus remote write 1.0, OTLP/HTTP (protobuf) and OTLP/gRPC.
  • Self-observability metrics, /healthz, /readyz, structured JSON logs.
  • Persistent state in SQLite (quota ledger, tokens, inventory cache, series registry).
  • Config hot reload on SIGHUP.
  • Simulator (tapyr sim) with fixtures, scenarios and limit enforcement; record mode (tapyr record) with anonymization.
  • Read-only status API (JSON, versioned) and read-only web UI embedded in the binary.
  • Four providers: teltonika-rms, teltonika-rutos, meraki-dashboard, aruba-central-classic.

Delivery:

  • Single static binary (Linux, macOS, Windows; amd64 and arm64), Docker image.
  • Demo docker compose: Tapyr + simulators + VictoriaMetrics + Grafana with provider dashboards and a "monitoring of monitoring" dashboard.
  • Generated JSON Schemas for editor autocompletion.
  • Documentation sources in docs/ (the documentation site docs.tapyr.eu is built from them after v0.1.0, ADR 0010).

items.title: Out of scope (keep in mind, do not build)
items.text:
• Distributed architecture (workers, sharding, leader election, HA).
  • Shared state backends (Redis) and persistent output buffering (WAL).
  • Editable UI, budget impact simulation in the UI, mapping authoring assistant.
  • Push-based sources: webhooks (Meraki), streaming APIs (Aruba Central websocket/protobuf).
  • Logs and events as outputs (metrics only).
  • Write operations against provider APIs.
  • Provider registry and distribution as OCI artifacts (phase 2 of the provider ecosystem, ADR 0011).
  • Generation of provider skeletons from OpenAPI specifications.
  • Aruba Central "new" (HPE GreenLake-based) provider.
  • Prometheus remote write 2.0.
  • Tracing of Tapyr runs (OpenTelemetry traces).

These items need an issue and an agreement before any code, but the design must not prevent them. In particular: the status API is the only interface the UI uses; state access goes through an interface so another backend can be added; outputs are pluggable; the provider package format is versioned.

items.title: Success criteria for v0.1.0
items.text:
• A new user runs the demo compose and sees data and self-metrics in Grafana within 5 minutes, without any vendor account.
  • tapyr plan on a Meraki or Aruba configuration gives a consumption estimate within 15% of the actual consumption measured against the simulator over 24 simulated hours.
  • Over a 24-hour simulated run with an undersized quota, Tapyr never receives an unexpected 429 from a quota limit (only from scenario-injected faults), degrades low-priority jobs first, and keeps critical jobs on schedule.
  • Teltonika RMS and Teltonika RutOS are validated end-to-end against real platforms.
  • Adding a simple new provider requires only YAML and CEL files, no Go code.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Tapyr is a single Go process. Configuration files are loaded and compiled into an in-memory runtime graph (providers, accounts, jobs, outputs). A scheduler triggers job runs; each run executes HTTP requests through the collection layer, which asks the budget engine for a reservation before every request. Responses are mapped by CEL into an internal metric model, then fanned out to the configured outputs. Everything is observable through self-metrics and a read-only status API, consumed by an embedded web UI.

                 ┌──────────────────────────── tapyr process ────────────────────────────┐
 config files ──▶│ config loader ─▶ compiler (schema + CEL type-check) ─▶ runtime graph   │
                 │                                                          │             │
                 │   planner ◀──────────── budget engine ◀───────┐          ▼             │
                 │      │                (ledger, buckets,       │      scheduler          │
                 │      ▼                 header sync)           │          │             │
                 │ effective intervals                           │          ▼             │
                 │                                               └── collection executor  │──▶ provider APIs
                 │                                          (auth, pagination, retries,   │    (or simulator)
                 │                                           circuit breaker)             │
                 │                                                          │             │
                 │                                                          ▼             │
                 │                                       mapping (CEL) ─▶ metric model     │
                 │                                                          │             │
                 │                          series registry (staleness, dedup)            │
                 │                                                          │             │
                 │                ┌────────────────┬───────────────┬────────┘             │
                 │                ▼                ▼               ▼                      │
                 │        prometheus pull   remote write        OTLP                      │──▶ TSDB / backends
                 │                                                                        │
                 │  state store (SQLite)   self-metrics   status API ─▶ embedded web UI   │
                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

items.title: Config loader and compiler (internal/config)
items.text:
• Loads one or more paths (files or directories, recursively *.yaml/*.yml), multi-document YAML.
  • Resolves built-in provider packages (embedded in the binary) and user provider packages (from providerPaths).
  • Validates every document against the JSON Schema of its kind, then performs semantic validation (references exist, no cycles in discovery, scopes reference known dimensions, limits are coherent).
  • Compiles every CEL expression against a declared environment and type-checks it.
  • Produces an immutable runtime.Graph. Hot reload builds a new graph and swaps it atomically; in-flight runs finish on the old graph.
  • Go types (and their doc comments, used as schema descriptions) are the single source of truth: JSON Schemas are generated from them (make schema), committed in schemas/, and embedded in the binary for validation and tapyr schema. A test fails when the committed schemas drift from the Go types.
  • Loading pipeline: YAML AST (positions kept) -> generic tree -> JSON Schema validation (errors mapped back to file:line:column) -> strict decoding into Go types -> defaults -> semantic validation.

items.title: Runtime compiler (internal/runtime)
items.text:
• Turns a validated configuration into the immutable runtime.Graph: CEL programs compiled, template fields evaluated per account and target, effective request, pagination, auth and labels resolved per job.
  • Used by validate (compilation errors with positions) and by run.

items.title: Secrets (internal/secret)
items.text: Resolved secret values are held in a type whose string, JSON and slog forms are [REDACTED], so they cannot leak through formatting by accident.

items.title: Provider registry (internal/provider)
items.text:
• Loads provider packages (see 03-configuration.md, "Provider packages").
  • Exposes provider definitions to the compiler and to the simulator.

items.title: Budget engine (internal/budget)
items.text: The heart of the project, see 04-budget-engine.md. Responsibilities: limit evaluation for each request, reservations, waiting, ledger persistence, header sync, 429 penalties, retry reserve, projections.

items.title: Planner (internal/budget/planner)
items.text: Computes effective intervals for all jobs given quotas, priorities and estimated calls per run. Used at startup, on reload, on inventory changes, periodically, and offline by tapyr plan.

items.title: Scheduler (internal/scheduler)
items.text:
• Triggers job runs according to effective intervals, with jitter to avoid synchronized bursts: every job instance gets a random phase in [0, jitter x interval) and runs at phase + k x interval, without drift.
  • Manages discovery fan-out: parent job results produce child run instances.
  • Enforces one run at a time per job instance (no overlap). If a run overruns its interval, the next run is skipped and counted.
  • Orders pending work by priority when the budget engine signals contention.

items.title: Collector (internal/collector)
items.text:
The process of tapyr run, wired by cmd/tapyr:

  • What outlives a configuration reload: the state store, the series registry, the outputs, the token sessions and the HTTP server (/metrics, /metrics/self, /healthz, /readyz, the status API and the UI).
  • A generation per compiled graph: its budget engine, executor, discovery and scheduler. A reload builds the next generation, stops the old one once its runs end, moves the ledger to the new engine, keeps the unchanged outputs and the schedule of the instances that stay, and retires the others.
  • The run of a job instance: the executor, the mapping, the inventory update, then the samples to the outputs and the run history.
  • Discovery: the children of every parent instance follow its inventory, start from the cached inventory after a restart, and are removed when it expires.
  • The online plan (every replanInterval, on a learned quota, on inventory changes, and when the current plan is projected to exhaust a quota), the flush loop (ledger, series, expiry), the push of the self-metrics, and the adapter of the status API.

items.title: Collection executor (internal/collect)
items.text:
• Builds requests from job definitions and variables, applies auth, handles pagination.
  • Calls the budget engine before every request (including pages, retries, token requests).
  • Classifies errors, applies the retry policy, and reports successes and transient failures to the circuit breakers, which live in the budget engine (one per account, or per target).
  • Returns the raw responses (all pages) for mapping, plus run statistics.

items.title: Auth (internal/auth)
items.text: Pluggable auth providers implementing a common interface (decorate a request, react to 401, refresh tokens). Declarative types plus Go plugins for flows that cannot be expressed declaratively (aruba_central_classic). Tokens are persisted in the state store when the flow requires it.

items.title: Mapping (internal/mapping)
items.text: Evaluates compiled CEL programs on responses to produce samples in the internal metric model. See 06-mapping-and-outputs.md.

items.title: Metric model and series registry (internal/model, internal/series)
items.text:
• Internal pivot model, close to the OpenTelemetry data model: metric name, type (gauge, counter), unit, description, labels (attributes), samples with optional source timestamps.
  • The series registry tracks, per job instance, the series seen in the last successful run and the last timestamp sent per series. It drives staleness and deduplication.

items.title: Outputs (internal/output)
items.text: Pluggable outputs, each with its own bounded in-memory queue and retry policy: prometheus (pull), remote_write, otlp. See 06-mapping-and-outputs.md.

items.title: State store (internal/state)
items.text: SQLite (modernc.org/sqlite, pure Go) behind a state.Store interface. Holds: quota ledger, auth tokens, inventory cache, series registry snapshots, run history (bounded). See "State" below.

items.title: Self-observability (internal/selfobs)
items.text: Self-metrics registry (Prometheus client_golang), health checks, structured logging setup. See 07-self-observability.md.

items.title: Status API and UI (internal/api, internal/ui, ui/)
items.text: Read-only JSON API under /api/v1, plus the embedded React UI served under /ui/. See 09-cli-api-ui.md.

items.title: Simulator (internal/sim)
items.text: HTTP server that serves provider fixtures and enforces provider limits, reusing the budget package server-side. See 08-simulator.md.

items.title: Request lifecycle
items.text:
1. The scheduler triggers run R of job J for account A (and target T if multi-target), with variables V (from discovery).
  2. The executor builds request 1 (method, URL template resolved with V, query, headers).
  3. The auth provider decorates the request. If a token is needed and absent or expired, the auth provider performs a token request, itself subject to a budget reservation against the provider's auth limits.
  4. The executor asks the budget engine to Reserve(descriptor). The descriptor carries provider, account, target, credential, templated endpoint, variables, job priority, and whether the request is a retry.
  5. The budget engine evaluates every limit whose scope matches, atomically. It returns a reservation, possibly after waiting (rate, concurrency), or a refusal (quota exhausted, scope penalized, circuit open) with a reason.
  6. The request is sent with a per-request timeout.
  7. On response, the executor reports the outcome to the budget engine (status code, quota headers, Retry-After), releases concurrency, and records self-metrics.
  8. Errors are classified; retryable errors re-enter step 4 as retries (consuming from the retry reserve).
  9. Pagination computes the next request (back to step 2) until done or maxPages.
  10. All pages are passed to the mapping, which produces samples.
  11. The series registry applies dedup and staleness, then samples are enqueued to the job's outputs.
  12. Run statistics are stored (run history) and exposed.

items.title: State
items.text:
Data Why persistent Notes Quota ledger (fixed and rolling windows) A restart must not reset daily or monthly consumption Rolling windows store per-minute buckets Auth tokens Rotating refresh tokens (Aruba Classic) are lost forever if not persisted Encrypted at rest with a key from TAPYR_STATE_KEY if set; warn if not set Inventory cache Avoid re-spending quota on discovery after restart TTL-based Series registry Staleness markers and dedup across restarts Snapshotted periodically Run history Status API and UI Bounded (last N runs per job)

Token buckets and concurrency counters are in-memory only (short horizon, safe to reset).

Tables: meta (key, value: schema version, credential salt, instance_id used as service.instance.id by OTLP), ledger (limit, scope key, window start, used, observed remaining, observed max, updated at), ledger_minutes (limit, scope key, minute, count: the buckets of rolling windows and of the current fixed window), runs (job, instance, run id, start, end, result, requests, pages, retries, items, samples, error; the last 50 per job instance), tokens (session key, sealed token, expiry; the key carries the provider, account, credential hash, target with perTarget, and a hash of the auth configuration, never a secret), inventory (job instance, item key, fields, updated at), series_instances (job instance, last success), series (job instance, output, series key, last source timestamp; rows with an empty output list the series of the last successful run) and accumulators (job instance, series key, total, last window) for reconstructed counters.

Hot reload (SIGHUP): the new configuration is loaded and compiled first; on any error it is rejected and logged, and the running graph stays. On success, scheduling of the old graph stops, its runs in flight finish, the budget engine is rebuilt with the ledger carried over, unchanged outputs are kept (the pull exposition keeps serving), removed job instances are retired, and the new graph starts. A reload never resets quota consumption.

The instances that stay keep their schedule: the new scheduler starts each one at the next run that was due in the old one (at once when it fell due during the reload, at most one new interval away when the interval shrank), so a reload neither loses nor adds runs and never postpones instances with long intervals. Children of fan-outs start again from the cached inventory. Token sessions are kept (a changed auth configuration opens a new one), run IDs continue one sequence per process, and the HTTP client is shared so that no connection is left behind. Changes to server, state.path and log settings are logged as taking effect after a restart. In flight runs get up to 30 seconds to finish before they are canceled.

The state file path defaults to ./data/tapyr.db. Writes are batched; the ledger is flushed at least every few seconds and on shutdown. Losing the last seconds of ledger updates is acceptable; quota header sync corrects drift.

items.title: Concurrency model
items.text:
• One goroutine pool for collection, bounded globally (settings.collection.maxConcurrentRequests) and further bounded by concurrency limits from providers.
  • Each output has its own sender goroutines and queue.
  • The budget engine is safe for concurrent use; reservations across multiple limits are atomic: every limit is acquired under the engine lock (no partial acquisition, no deadlock; see 04-budget-engine.md).
  • Graceful shutdown: stop scheduling, wait for in-flight runs up to a timeout, flush outputs up to a timeout, flush state, exit.

items.title: Main dependencies
items.text: Concern Library CLI github.com/spf13/cobra YAML github.com/goccy/go-yaml (good error positions) JSON Schema generation github.com/invopop/jsonschema JSON Schema validation github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 CEL cel.dev/cel-go SQLite modernc.org/sqlite (no CGO) Prometheus exposition and self-metrics github.com/prometheus/client_golang Remote write minimal protos encoded with google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protowire, compressed with github.com/klauspost/compress/snappy OTLP go.opentelemetry.io/collector/pdata (pmetric payloads built directly), sent over OTLP/HTTP or gRPC (google.golang.org/grpc) Logging log/slog (standard library) UI React, Vite, TypeScript, @xyflow/react (graph); charts are hand-written SVG Release GoReleaser Lint golangci-lint

items.title: Principles
items.text:
• YAML, multi-document, Kubernetes-like envelope: apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec.
  • apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1 for every document.
  • Documents can be spread across any number of files and directories. Tapyr loads all of them and resolves references by name.
  • Every kind has a JSON Schema generated from Go types, published in schemas/v1alpha1/ and printable with tapyr schema; the configuration reference lists every field, generated from the same types. schemas/v1alpha1/tapyr.json accepts any kind (dispatched on kind) and is meant for editors, for example with the YAML language server: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kentrow/tapyr/main/schemas/v1alpha1/tapyr.json.
  • Secrets are never inline. They are references to environment variables or files.
  • Durations use Go syntax (30s, 5m, 1h). Rates use <n>/<unit> with unit s, m or h (10/s, 600/m). Percentages are strings "<n>%" (10%, 2.5%). Ratios such as budget.share are plain numbers.
  • Names are DNS-label-like: lowercase, digits, hyphens, max 63 characters. metadata.name is unique per kind across the whole configuration (provider packages conventionally prefix their template names with the package name). Limit names are unique per provider, target names per account; both follow the same DNS-label rule.
  • Identifiers used inside expressions and path templates (params, secrets, variables) match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ (apiKey, organizationId), so they are usable as vars.organizationId in CEL and {organizationId} in paths.
  • Parsing is strict: unknown fields are errors, except inside free-form maps (labels, params, headers, externalLabels, resourceAttributes, plugin config). Values of string maps must be YAML strings: port: 8080 or country: NO are rejected with a hint to quote the value ("8080", "NO").
  • Relative paths written in a document (file secrets, caFile, providerPaths, state.path, TLS files) are resolved against the directory of the file that declares them. Built-in defaults (./data/tapyr.db) are resolved against the working directory.
  • Errors are reported as file:line:column: message, all at once (validation does not stop at the first error).

items.title: Value types
items.text:
Three syntaxes coexist, each confined to well-defined fields:

Syntax Where Evaluated Go text/template ({{ .params.baseURL }}) Fields documented as templates: Provider.spec.baseURL, Provider.spec.defaults.headers values, oauth2ClientCredentials.tokenURL Once per account and target, at compile time. .params is the account params overridden by the target params. Functions: default, trimSuffix, lower, upper {name} placeholders request.path, sessionLogin.request.path Per request, from variables (discovery vars, then target params, then account params). Values are URL-path-escaped CEL Fields documented as expressions (extract.*, forEach.vars, pagination stop/total/cursor/next, ...) and { expr: ... } values At runtime

Secret and value references:

  • SecretRef (user side: Account, Output, Settings): exactly one of { env: NAME } or { file: /path }. Secrets are never written inline.
  • Value (provider and job side): a plain string (literal), { secret: <name> } (a secret declared by the provider and supplied by the account), or { expr: <cel> }. In auth blocks, a Value is a literal or a secret reference only: credentials are resolved once per account, before any request, so there is nothing for an expression to read (tapyr validate rejects one).
  • Header values in outputs: a plain string (literal) or a SecretRef.

items.title: Kinds
items.text:
Kind Who writes it Purpose Provider Provider package author API family: base URL template, auth, limits, pagination, error semantics JobTemplate Provider package author Reusable, provider-level job definitions (endpoint + mapping) Account User Instance of a provider with credentials, targets, labels, budget share Job User What to collect for which account: either from a JobTemplate or fully custom Output User Where data goes Settings User Global settings (server, state, collection defaults); at most one document

Simulation and Scenario (see 08-simulator.md) also use apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1, but they are internal to provider packages (sim/ directory) and are rejected with an explicit error when found in user configuration paths.

items.title: Provider
items.text:
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Provider
metadata:
  name: meraki-dashboard
  version: 0.1.0                       # provider package version (semver)
  description: Cisco Meraki Dashboard API v1
  docs: https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api-v1/
  # Catalog metadata (ADR 0011): optional, required by tapyr provider lint --catalog
  displayName: Cisco Meraki Dashboard
  categories: [network, wireless, sd-wan]   # from providers/categories.yaml, the main one first
  maintainers: [Kentrow]               # GitHub handles, without @
  tier: official                       # official | community
  validation:
    status: simulator                  # simulator | real-platform
    # date: 2026-11-04                 # YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM; with platformVersion, required for real-platform
    # platformVersion: Dashboard API v1.75.1
    notes: Built from the official documentation and OpenAPI description v1.75.1
spec:
  baseURL: "{{ .params.baseURL | default \"https://api.meraki.com/api/v1\" }}"

  params:                              # parameters an Account may or must provide
    - name: baseURL
      required: false
      description: Regional base URL

  secrets:                             # secrets an Account must provide
    - name: apiKey
      required: true

  auth:
    type: bearer
    bearer:
      token: { secret: apiKey }

  defaults:
    headers:
      Accept: application/json
    timeout: 30s

  pagination:                          # default pagination, overridable per job template
    type: link_header
    linkHeader:
      pageSizeParam: perPage
      pageSize: 1000

  limits:
    - name: org-rate
      description: Per-organization throughput
      source:                          # optional, required by tapyr provider lint --catalog
        kind: vendor-docs              # vendor-docs (with url) | measured (with date) | assumed
        url: https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api-v1/rate-limit/
        date: 2026-11-04               # when the source was checked or the measurement made
      kind: rate
      rate: 10/s
      burst: 10
      scope: { by: [account, "var:organizationId"] }
      appliesTo: { requestsWithVar: organizationId }

    - name: ip-rate
      kind: rate
      rate: 100/s
      scope: { by: [instance] }

    - name: ip-concurrency
      kind: concurrency
      max: 10
      scope: { by: [instance] }

  errors:
    rateLimited:
      statuses: [429]
      retryAfterHeader: Retry-After
    authFailed:
      statuses: [401]
    retryable:
      statuses: [500, 502, 503, 504]
  redirects:                          # optional: other hosts requests may be redirected to
    hosts: ["*.example.com"]          # see "Redirects" in 05-collection.md

Notes:

  • String fields marked as templates use Go text/template with a restricted function set (default, trimSuffix, lower, upper), evaluated at compile time per account and target (see "Value types"). Runtime expressions use CEL.
  • limits are described in detail in 04-budget-engine.md.
  • errors declares the provider's error semantics; defaults apply when omitted: rateLimited (statuses: [429], retryAfterHeader: Retry-After, defaultPenalty: 2s, penalize: narrowest), authFailed (statuses: [401]), retryable (statuses: [500, 502, 503, 504]). penalize is narrowest or all (see 04-budget-engine.md, "429 handling").
  • auth.type is one of none, header, bearer, basic, oauth2_client_credentials, session_login, plugin. The configuration block of a type is named after the type in camelCase (bearer, oauth2ClientCredentials, sessionLogin, plugin). Pagination follows the same rule (linkHeader for link_header).
  • Auth plugins (Go code, for flows that cannot be expressed declaratively) are selected with type: plugin and plugin: { name: <plugin>, config: {...} }. The core schema treats config as free-form; the plugin validates it at compile time. This keeps vendor names out of the core schema.
  • params and secrets declare what an Account may or must provide. An Account providing an undeclared param or secret is an error.
  • The catalog metadata (displayName, categories, maintainers, tier, validation) and the source of the limits describe the package for the provider catalog (ADR 0011); the engine ignores them. Two axes describe a package: tier says who maintains it (official: the Tapyr maintainers, community: the maintainers listed), validation how it was last tested. They are optional, so that user packages need none; tapyr provider lint --catalog requires them (see Provider packages).

items.title: JobTemplate
items.text:
A provider package ships job templates so users get a working setup with a few lines.

apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: JobTemplate
metadata:
  name: meraki-organizations
spec:
  provider: meraki-dashboard
  role: inventory                       # inventory | metrics | both (default metrics)
  defaultInterval: 6h
  defaultPriority: low
  request:
    method: GET
    path: /organizations
  extract:
    items: "response.body"
    inventory:
      key: "item.id"
      fields:
        organizationId: "item.id"
        organizationName: "item.name"

---
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: JobTemplate
metadata:
  name: meraki-device-statuses
spec:
  provider: meraki-dashboard
  defaultInterval: 5m
  defaultPriority: high
  forEach:
    template: meraki-organizations      # fan out over the parent's inventory items
    vars:
      organizationId: "parent.organizationId"
  request:
    method: GET
    path: /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/statuses
  estimate:
    pagesPerRun: 1                      # hint for the planner before history exists
  extract:
    items: "response.body"
    metrics:
      - name: meraki_device_up
        type: gauge
        help: Device online status (1 online, 0 otherwise)
        value: "item.status == 'online' ? 1.0 : 0.0"
        labels:
          serial: "item.serial"
          network_id: "item.networkId"
          organization_id: "vars.organizationId"
    info:
      - name: meraki_device_info
        labels:
          serial: "item.serial"
          name: "item.name"
          model: "item.model"
          product_type: "item.productType"
          lan_ip: "has(item.lanIp) ? item.lanIp : ''"

items.title: Account
items.text:
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Account
metadata:
  name: acme-meraki
spec:
  provider: meraki-dashboard
  params:
    baseURL: https://api.meraki.com/api/v1
  secrets:
    apiKey: { env: TAPYR_ACME_MERAKI_API_KEY }
  labels:                               # added to every sample from this account
    tenant: acme
  budget:
    share: 0.7                          # Tapyr may use 70% of quota-type limits (others share the key)

Multi-target account (one account, N devices):

apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Account
metadata:
  name: branch-routers
spec:
  provider: teltonika-rutos
  secrets:
    username: { env: TAPYR_RUTOS_USER }
    password: { file: /run/secrets/rutos_password }
  targets:
    - name: north-01
      params: { baseURL: "https://10.10.1.1" }
      labels: { site: north }
    - name: south-01
      params: { baseURL: "https://10.20.1.1" }
      labels: { site: south }
      secrets:                          # per-target override
        password: { env: TAPYR_RUTOS_SOUTH_PASSWORD }
  tls:
    insecureSkipVerify: false
    caFile: /etc/tapyr/rutos-ca.pem
  • Jobs on a multi-target account run once per target. The target scope dimension lets providers declare per-device limits.
  • Secret references: { env: NAME }, { file: /path }. File secrets are re-read on reload.
  • budget.share (0 < share <= 1, default 1) scales every quota limit for this account. Rate and concurrency limits are not scaled by default; budget.scaleRates: true scales them too (rate, burst and concurrency max, rounded down, minimum 1). When a scope key is shared by several accounts (for example an instance or credential scope), the smallest share among them applies.
  • Required params must be provided by the account or by every target. Required secrets must be provided by the account or by every target (target secrets override account secrets).

items.title: Job
items.text:
From a template:

apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: acme-device-statuses
spec:
  account: acme-meraki
  template: meraki-device-statuses
  interval: 5m                          # desired interval (planner may stretch it)
  priority: critical                    # critical | high | normal | low
  outputs: [victoria]                   # default: all outputs
  labels: { env: prod }

When a template uses forEach over a parent template, Tapyr automatically instantiates the parent as an implicit inventory job for the same account if no explicit job references it. Users can declare it explicitly to override its interval.

A Job either references a template or carries an inline definition, never both:

  • With template, the job may only set interval (default: the template's defaultInterval), priority (default: the template's defaultPriority), outputs, labels and staleAfter. Definition fields (role, request, pagination, forEach, estimate, extract) are rejected.
  • Without template, the job carries the same definition fields as a JobTemplate spec, interval is required and priority defaults to normal.

The definition fields shared by JobTemplate and inline Job:

Field Content role inventory, metrics (default) or both request method (default GET), path (with {var} placeholders), query (map of Value), headers (map of strings), body (map of Value, POST queries only), readOnly (required true for POST), idempotent (POST retried only if true), timeout pagination Overrides the provider default (see 05-collection.md). Every type accepts maxPages (default 100) forEach template (a parent JobTemplate) or job (a parent Job of the same account), exactly one; vars (map of CEL on parent), filter (CEL), maxInstances (default 10000). The parent must have role: inventory or both estimate pagesPerRun (planner hint) extract items, filter, partial, metrics, info, inventory (key, fields, ttl), post (see 06-mapping-and-outputs.md)

Fully custom job (no template):

apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: rms-devices
spec:
  account: home-rms
  interval: 10m
  priority: normal
  request:
    method: GET
    path: /devices
    query:
      limit: "100"
  pagination:
    type: offset
    offset:
      offsetParam: offset
      limitParam: limit
      pageSize: 100
      stop: "size(response.body.data) < 100"
  extract:
    items: "response.body.data"
    metrics:
      - name: teltonika_rms_device_online
        type: gauge
        value: "item.status == 1 ? 1.0 : 0.0"
        labels:
          device_id: "string(item.id)"
          name: "item.name"

items.title: Output
items.text:
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Output
metadata:
  name: victoria
spec:
  type: remote_write
  remoteWrite:
    url: http://victoriametrics:8428/api/v1/write
    headers: {}
    basicAuth: { username: { env: VM_USER }, password: { env: VM_PASSWORD } }
    timeout: 10s
  queue:
    capacity: 50000                     # samples
    maxBatch: 5000
    flushInterval: 5s
  externalLabels:
    tapyr_instance: lab
  processing:                           # for this output only, metric_relabel_configs semantics (ADR 0012)
    - action: drop
      sourceLabels: [__name__]
      regex: "meraki_uplink_.*"
    - action: labeldrop
      regex: firmware
---
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Output
metadata:
  name: prom
spec:
  type: prometheus                       # served on the main server under /metrics
  prometheus:
    exposeTimestamps: false
---
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Output
metadata:
  name: otel
spec:
  type: otlp
  otlp:
    endpoint: http://otel-collector:4318
    protocol: http/protobuf              # http/protobuf | grpc
    headers: {}
    resourceAttributes:
      service.name: tapyr
  • At most one prometheus output may be declared (it is served on the main server under /metrics). queue applies to push outputs only and is rejected on prometheus.
  • Queue defaults: capacity: 50000, maxBatch: 5000, flushInterval: 5s. Timeout default: 10s.
  • Header values are plain strings or SecretRefs (X-Scope-OrgID: tenant-a, Authorization: { env: OTLP_TOKEN }).

items.title: Settings
items.text:
apiVersion: tapyr/v1alpha1
kind: Settings
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  server:
    listen: 127.0.0.1:9790
    basicAuth:
      username: { env: TAPYR_UI_USER }
      password: { env: TAPYR_UI_PASSWORD }
      protectMetrics: false              # also protect /metrics and /metrics/self
    # tls: { certFile: /etc/tapyr/tls.crt, keyFile: /etc/tapyr/tls.key }
    ui: { enabled: true }
    debug:                               # live debug endpoint (raw responses)
      enabled: false
      maxBodyBytes: 1048576
  state:
    path: ./data/tapyr.db
  providerPaths:
    - ./providers                        # user provider packages, in addition to built-ins
  collection:
    maxConcurrentRequests: 32
    defaultTimeout: 30s
    jitter: 10%
  budget:
    retryReserve: 10%                    # 0% to 50%
    replanInterval: 15m
    replanOnProjection: true             # replan at once when the plan would exhaust a quota before its reset
    maxStretch: 12                       # planner stretch cap per priority class
  retry:
    maxAttempts: 4
    initialBackoff: 1s
    maxBackoff: 60s
    multiplier: 2
  circuitBreaker:
    failureThreshold: 5
    cooldown: 2m
    maxCooldown: 30m                     # cooldown doubles on repeated openings up to this value
  mapping:
    maxCost: 1000000                     # CEL cost limit per expression evaluation
    maxItemsPerRun: 100000
    maxSamplesPerRun: 200000
    labelConflict: override              # override (job > target > account > mapping) | error
  selfMetrics:
    outputs: []                          # optionally push self-metrics through these outputs
    interval: 30s                        # push interval of the self-metrics
  log:
    level: info
    format: json

All settings have defaults; the Settings document is optional. collection.jitter is in [0%, 50%].

Logging precedence: --log-level / --log-format flags, then TAPYR_LOG_LEVEL / TAPYR_LOG_FORMAT, then Settings.spec.log, then defaults. A bootstrap logger built from flags and environment is used until the configuration is loaded.

items.title: Provider packages
items.text:
A provider package is a directory named after its provider:

providers/<name>/
├── provider.yaml          # Provider (exactly one): base URL, params, secrets, auth, pagination, limits, errors
├── templates/*.yaml       # JobTemplates: request, estimate.pagesPerRun, CEL extract
├── sim/sim.yaml           # Simulation (see 08-simulator.md): inventory, routes, fixtures, auth accepted
├── sim/fixtures/          # static fixtures or Go templates (*.tmpl)
├── sim/scenarios/         # default.yaml, quota-tight.yaml, bad-day.yaml (all three required)
├── tests/contract.yaml    # jobs run once against the simulator
├── tests/contract.env     # the simulator credentials for the contract test
├── tests/expected.prom    # the samples they must produce
├── dashboards/*.json      # Grafana dashboard(s) with a datasource variable
├── examples/*.yaml        # example Account and Job documents that load
└── README.md              # coverage, auth setup, limits with sources, validation status, caveats
  • metadata.version is semver. Breaking changes to metric names or labels bump the major version.
  • Built-in packages are embedded in the binary. User packages from providerPaths override built-ins with the same name (with a warning).
  • Precedence, highest first: Provider documents written directly in the configuration paths, then packages from providerPaths (in order), then built-in packages. A package that is overridden is dropped entirely, its job templates included. Every override is reported as a warning by validate and run.
  • Each providerPaths entry is either a package directory (it contains provider.yaml) or a directory of packages (each subdirectory containing a provider.yaml is a package).
  • In a package, provider.yaml holds exactly one Provider, templates/*.yaml hold only JobTemplate documents whose spec.provider is the package name, and sim/sim.yaml holds at most one Simulation. The package directory name must equal the provider name.
  • tapyr provider lint <dir> validates a package and runs its contract test (see 08-simulator.md). With --catalog, it also requires the catalog metadata: a displayName, at least one category of providers/categories.yaml, at least one maintainer, a tier, a validation (with its date and platformVersion when its status is real-platform), and a source on every limit (with its url for vendor-docs, its date for measured); dates must exist. The CI runs it on the built-in packages.

items.title: Validation rules (non-exhaustive)
items.text:
