The CI runs the lint of every built-in package, with --catalog (03-configuration.md).
  • Dashboards (dashboards/*.json, Grafana) must parse, use a datasource variable, and query only metrics produced by the package templates or tapyr_ self-metrics.

items.title: Future
items.text:
• Provider packages distributed with their simulator as OCI artifacts, community registry.
  • Simulator scenarios composable across providers for lab use (e.g. a shared "branch office outage" timeline).

items.title: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: CLI
items.text:
Single binary tapyr, built with cobra. Global flags: --config <path> (repeatable, files or directories; env TAPYR_CONFIG, a list separated by the OS path list separator, : on Unix and ; on Windows), --log-level, --log-format (env TAPYR_LOG_LEVEL, TAPYR_LOG_FORMAT). Flags win over environment variables.

Common exit codes: 0 success, 1 usage error or internal error, 2 invalid configuration (including missing files and YAML syntax errors), 3 infeasible plan.

Command Purpose Exit codes tapyr run Run the collector (server, scheduler, outputs) 0 on clean shutdown, 1 on fatal error tapyr validate [--check-secrets] [--provider-path DIR ...] Load, schema-validate, semantic-validate, compile CEL; optionally resolve secrets 0 valid, 2 invalid (errors with file:line:column) tapyr plan [--fanout tmpl=N ...] [--output table\|json] [--provider-path DIR ...] Compute effective intervals and projected consumption per quota scope, offline. Uses the state store inventory and run history if present 0 feasible, 3 infeasible tapyr sim ... Run provider simulators (see 08-simulator.md) tapyr record --job J [--job ...] --out DIR [--anonymize FILE] [--provider-path DIR ...] Run jobs once and record their responses, anonymized (see 08-simulator.md) 0 ok, 1 error, 2 invalid configuration tapyr schema [--kind K] [--out dir] Print or write the JSON Schemas embedded in the binary tapyr provider list [--output table\|json] List built-in and user provider packages with versions; json is the provider catalog output tapyr provider lint <dir> [--update] [--catalog] Validate a provider package, lint its dashboards and run its contract tests (--update rewrites tests/expected.prom, --catalog also requires the catalog metadata) 0 ok, 2 errors tapyr version Version, revision, Go version

--provider-path (validate, plan, record, and sim) loads the provider packages of a directory in addition to the built-in ones and to the providerPaths of the configuration, after the latter: it serves a package being written, before it is built in or referenced by a configuration.

Signals for run: SIGHUP reloads the configuration (validated first; an invalid config is rejected and the running config kept); SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger graceful shutdown.

tapyr plan reads run history and inventory from the state store when the file exists (read-only); otherwise it uses estimate.pagesPerRun and the --fanout hints. Quotas are evaluated over a full window from now: plan answers "does this configuration fit", while the running engine replans with the remaining budget of the current window.

Example tapyr plan output, for the example configuration of the aruba-central-classic package (a job stretched to fit a quota shows its stretch factor and reason):

QUOTA SCOPE                  WINDOW       BUDGET         PROJECTED                RESERVE  STATUS
aruba-central-classic/daily  24h          4500           529                      500      ok (11.8%)
  account=campus
  job aruba-aps              desired 5m   effective 5m   288 runs x 1 page = 302
  job aruba-gateways         desired 15m  effective 15m  96 runs x 1 page = 101
  job aruba-sites            desired 1h   effective 1h   24 runs x 1 page = 25
  job aruba-switches         desired 15m  effective 15m  96 runs x 1 page = 101
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Provider catalog output
items.text:
tapyr provider list --output json describes the packages the command lists, in precedence order, for the provider catalog of tapyr.eu (ADR 0011): the site repository builds the catalog from the output of a tagged release, as it builds the documentation from docsite export (ADR 0010). It is an interface of the site repository. The keys are the camelCase names of the configuration fields they come from; an optional field without a value is left out.

  • schemaVersion (1): changes when a field is removed, renamed or changes meaning, never when one is added. Readers ignore unknown fields.
  • tapyrVersion: the version of the binary.
  • categories: the controlled vocabulary of providers/categories.yaml, name and description.
  • providers: one entry per package:
  • from metadata: name, version, displayName, description, docs, categories, maintainers, tier, validation (status, date, platformVersion, notes);
  • origin: builtin, or the directory of a user package; status: active, or overridden by a package of the same name listed before it;
  • readme: for a built-in package, the path of its README in this repository (providers/<name>/README.md); the site maps it to the page of the documentation version it publishes;
  • simulator: whether the package has one; auth: the auth type, plugin:<name> for an auth plugin;
  • templates: name, description, the request path, defaultInterval (5m, 1h) and the sorted metrics names it produces;
  • limits: name, kind, value (for humans, defaults applied: 10/s, burst 20, 4 concurrent requests, 100000 per month, reset on day 1 at 00:00 UTC, auto (5000 until learned) per day, reset at 00:00 UTC), scope (the dimensions of scope.by), description and source (kind, url, date).

The output of the built-in packages is kept in cmd/tapyr/testdata/provider-list.json (go test ./cmd/tapyr -run TestProviderListJSON -update), so that a change of the interface shows in the diff of a pull request.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: HTTP server
items.text:
One listener (settings.server.listen, default 127.0.0.1:9790) serving:

Path Content /metrics Collected data (prometheus output) /metrics/self Self-metrics /healthz, /readyz Health /api/v1/... Status API (read-only, JSON) /ui/ Embedded web UI (redirect / to /ui/)

Optional basic auth (settings.server.basicAuth) protects /api and /ui (and optionally /metrics* with settings.server.basicAuth.protectMetrics: true). Put Tapyr behind a reverse proxy for TLS, or set settings.server.tls (certFile, keyFile) to serve HTTPS directly.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Status API
items.text:
Read-only, JSON, versioned under /api/v1. It is the only interface the UI uses. An OpenAPI 3 description is maintained by hand in internal/api/openapi.yaml and served at /api/v1/openapi.yaml.

Endpoint Content GET /api/v1/status Version, uptime, config hash, last reload result and errors, readiness reasons, plan feasibility GET /api/v1/providers Providers with package version, accounts count, health summary GET /api/v1/accounts / {name} Accounts (no secrets), targets, labels, circuit state, auth status, health and its reasons GET /api/v1/jobs / {name} Effective config (after defaults and template expansion), desired and effective intervals, instances, last run summary, next run GET /api/v1/jobs/{name}/instances Fan-out instances with their variables and last result GET /api/v1/jobs/{name}/runs?instance= Recent runs with statistics and redacted errors GET /api/v1/budgets Every limit and scope key: kind, max, used, remaining (internal and observed), external usage, reserve, window bounds, projection, and the accounts whose requests count in the scope (named by its account, target or credential dimension; every account of the provider for a scope without one) GET /api/v1/budgets/{limit}/timeline?scope= {limit} is provider/limit, URL-encoded (meraki-dashboard%2Fdaily). Consumption time series for the current and previous window (per-minute buckets from the ledger) GET /api/v1/plan The current plan (same data as tapyr plan) GET /api/v1/graph Nodes and edges: provider, account, target, job, job instance groups, output GET /api/v1/outputs Outputs with queue state and last send results GET /api/v1/debug/jobs/{name}/last?instance= Last raw response pages (redacted, truncated to settings.server.debug.maxBodyBytes, default 1 MiB) and the samples produced. Only when settings.server.debug.enabled GET /api/v1/events Server-Sent Events stream: run finished, plan changed, circuit changed, config reloaded

Rules: never expose secrets; redact headers as in logs; paginate list endpoints (?limit=&cursor=); stable field names (snake_case); ISO 8601 timestamps.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Health
items.text:
Every job, account and provider has a health: ok, degraded, failing, or unknown before its first run. Parts combine the same way at every level: ok or failing when every known part is, degraded when they differ, unknown parts left out.

  • Run: success is ok, failed is failing; partial and the skipped runs (skipped_budget, skipped_overlap, skipped_circuit) are degraded: nothing failed, but not everything was collected.
  • Job: the last runs of its instances.
  • Account: the last runs of its job instances, made worse by its credentials (a manual re-bootstrap required fails it) and by its circuits (open for the account or for every target fails it; open for some targets, or half open, degrades it). health_reasons says why, when it is not ok: the redacted errors of its jobs (the jobs that share an error share a reason, three reasons at most, then how many more), the re-bootstrap, the open circuits. A rejected key shows as a failing account with the 401 of its jobs.
  • Provider: its accounts. One account failing out of several degrades the provider instead of failing it.

The Overview lists the accounts that are not ok with their reasons, and the Graph colors the account nodes with their health and shows the reasons in the detail panel.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Implementation notes
items.text:
• internal/api serves the API from a read-only Source interface implemented by tapyr run; it never reaches into the collector state directly. The OpenAPI description (OpenAPI 3.1) is maintained by hand; a test checks that every route is documented and that every response of the test suite validates against its schema.
  • Pagination: limit (default 100, at most 1000) and an opaque cursor; responses of list endpoints are {"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}, next_cursor omitted on the last page.
  • Errors are {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."}} with the matching HTTP status.
  • Budget timelines use buckets of 1 minute for windows up to one day and of 1 hour beyond; the current window's buckets are persisted with the ledger, the previous window's are kept in memory only.
  • Basic auth compares in constant time and answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate; /healthz and /readyz are never protected. With tls, the listener serves HTTPS only.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Web UI (read-only)
items.text: Inspired by the Grafana Alloy UI: see what is configured and how it behaves, never edit.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Technology
items.text:
React + Vite + TypeScript, compiled to static assets in ui/dist/app, embedded with go:embed by ui/embed.go and served by internal/ui. Graph rendering with @xyflow/react. Budget timelines and gauges are hand-written SVG. No server-side rendering. In development, Vite proxies /api to a running tapyr run.

The UI is built in CI and in make build; a binary built without UI assets serves a minimal page explaining how to build them.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Pages
items.text:
1. Overview: health summary, plan feasibility banner, providers and accounts cards with status, quota gauges (used / projected / limit per window, named by the accounts of their scope), recent errors.
  2. Graph: provider -> account -> (targets) -> inventory jobs -> metric jobs -> outputs. Node color by health. Click a node to open its detail panel. Fan-out shown as grouped nodes with instance counts.
  3. Job detail: effective config (YAML view), desired vs effective interval with stretch reason, instances table, recent runs (result, duration, requests, pages, retries, samples), errors.
  4. Budgets: one card per limit and scope: timeline of consumption over the window with projection line, reserve, external usage, window reset time. Rate limits show wait time and 429s.
  5. Plan: the plan table, sortable, with stretched jobs highlighted.
  6. Outputs: queue fill, send rate, failures, last success.
  7. Live debug (only when enabled): pick a job instance, see the last raw response (pretty JSON, collapsible) side by side with the samples produced. Refresh on new run (SSE).

Every page shows, at the foot of the navigation, the version of the running Tapyr (Tapyr v0.3.0; a binary built without a version, such as go build in a clone, shows Tapyr dev and its short revision), with the full version, the revision and the Go version in its tooltip. It is read from GET /api/v1/status when the UI loads and again when the event stream reconnects, so an upgrade shows after the restart.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Non-functional
items.text:
• Responsive down to tablet width; usable on a phone for the overview.
  • Light and dark themes (follows the system preference).
  • Live updates via SSE, with polling fallback.
  • No external network calls (fonts and assets bundled).
  • Accessible: keyboard navigation, sufficient contrast, no information conveyed by color alone.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: Implementation notes
items.text:
• Serving. The UI is served under /ui/ (/ redirects there) with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none' (the CSP constant of internal/ui), so that the browser itself refuses any external call; settings.server.ui.enabled: false removes it. Hashed assets are cached for a year, index.html is never cached. A binary built without the UI serves a page explaining make ui.
  • Events. GET /api/v1/events is a Server-Sent Events stream of run_finished (job, instance, result, duration, samples), plan_changed, circuit_changed (account, target, state) and config_reloaded (result, error), each data a JSON object with time. A comment line is sent every 15 seconds to keep proxies from closing the stream. Slow clients lose events rather than slowing the collector: the UI refetches what it shows on every event and polls every 15 seconds when the stream is down.
  • Debug. With settings.server.debug.enabled, the collector keeps, per job instance and in memory only, the pages of its last run (status, the Content-Type and quota headers, the body truncated to maxBodyBytes) and the samples it produced. Bodies go through the log redactor, so configured secrets and tokens never appear. Without it, the endpoint answers 404 with the code debug_disabled.
  • Look. The colors, fonts and shapes follow tapyr.eu: background #f2f8fb / #0b1824, surface #ffffff / #102335, ink #0f2a3f / #e4f1f7, cyan #3aa9d6 / #5cc3ea, sun #ffc845 / #ffd166, red #cc2f35 / #ff7a7a; Bricolage Grotesque for titles, JetBrains Mono for data. States always carry a word or an icon next to their color.
path: 09 - CLI, status API and web UI

items.title: 10 - Built-in providers
items.text:
The built-in provider packages. Each section was checked against the vendor documentation (and, where its section says so, the real platform) in November 2026; each package README cites the source of every declared limit.

Package Kind of API Testing What it validates teltonika-rms Cloud, central Real platform (maintainer access) + simulator The whole pipeline against a real platform teltonika-rutos Local device API, multi-target, session auth Real devices + simulator Validates multi-target accounts and session_login meraki-dashboard Cloud, per-org rate limits, Link pagination DevNet sandbox (e2e) + simulator (docs + public OpenAPI spec) Validates scoped rate limits and discovery chains aruba-central-classic Cloud, daily quota, rotating refresh tokens Real account, read-only (November 2026) + simulator Validates quota windows, header sync, auth plugin juniper-mist Cloud, hourly quota per token, regional clouds Simulator only (docs + public OpenAPI spec) Validates header auth with a format, page pagination, hourly windows cisco-thousandeyes Cloud, per-minute quota per organization starting at the first request Simulator only (docs + official SDKs) Validates windows followed through the reset header, source timestamps per round, optional query params unifi-site-manager Cloud, one API key for every console of a UI account, rate limit per key Real account, read-only (November 2026) + simulator Validates cursor pagination in the body, windows published late with source timestamps, several item kinds from one response

items.title: teltonika-rms
items.text:
Teltonika Remote Management System, cloud API. Checked in November 2026 against the API documentation, its OpenAPI description (version 3.0.0, "v3-BETA": additive changes that may still break clients) and the real platform.

  • Auth: personal access token (created under Account settings > API, requires 2FA, shown once) as Authorization: Bearer <token>, scope devices:read (authentication, scopes). OAuth (authorization code with PKCE) exists for multi-user apps; not needed.
  • Base URL: https://api.rms.teltonika-networks.com (the OpenAPI servers entry https://rms.teltonika-networks.com/api serves the same API). No version segment.
  • Rate limits: documented as 100 000 requests per month per application, 429 with Retry-After. Measured on the platform (2026-11-03): every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit (100000), X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch seconds), and the reset was one month after the first request of the window, not a calendar month. Declared as a month quota with max: auto synced from the three headers (the reset header sets the window end), plus a conservative rate: 2/s (assumed, none documented).
  • Pagination: offset / limit (default 10, no documented maximum: the templates use 100), total in meta.total. Lists accept fields= to select fields and filters such as status=online.
  • Envelope: {"success": true, "data": [...], "meta": {"total": N}}; errors {"success": false, "errors": [{"code": "UNAUTHORIZED", "message": "..."}]}. Timestamps are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS strings in UTC.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • rms-devices (GET /devices, inventory and metrics in one paginated call, the mobile signal of the first modem included, so no per-device call is needed);
  • rms-device-data-usage (GET /devices/{id}/data-usage, one call per device, 6h interval; the README gives the monthly cost per device).
  • Freshness: RMS data is as fresh as each device reports it (dynamic_monitoring, often 300 s); polling faster than that only spends quota.
  • Deliverables: provider package, simulator fixtures built from anonymized recordings (tapyr record), dashboard, e2e test behind the e2e build tag.

items.title: teltonika-rutos
items.text:
Local REST API of Teltonika routers running RutOS. Checked in November 2026 against the RutOS API documentation (OpenAPI descriptions per firmware, from 7.6 to 7.26.1).

  • Firmware: the REST API exists from RutOS 07.06 (Teltonika community); the package targets 07.06 and later. Base path /api (the latest API version; /api/v1 pins it). The legacy ubus JSON-RPC API is not supported.
  • Auth: POST /api/login with {"username": ..., "password": ...} answers {"success": true, "data": {"username": ..., "token": ..., "expires": 299}}; the token is a bearer token valid 5 minutes by default (api_session_timeout). POST /api/logout closes the session: RutOS keeps expired sessions open and its memory grows when a client logs in repeatedly (Teltonika community), so the package declares logout. Implemented with session_login, perTarget: true. A dedicated user in a group with read access only is recommended.
  • TLS: HTTPS with a self-signed certificate is the default from 07.12 (RUTX) and 07.15 (other models); accounts use tls.caFile or, explicitly, tls.insecureSkipVerify.
  • Rate limits: none documented; devices are resource-constrained. Declared: concurrency: 2 and rate: 2/s per target (assumed).
  • Envelope: {"success": true, "data": ...}; errors {"success": false, "errors": [{"code": 120, "error": "...", "source": "...", "section": "..."}]} (120 unauthorized, 121 login failed). Payloads may change between firmware versions; templates read current field names with fallbacks to the 7.6 names (signal, oper, state).
  • Multi-target: one Account lists the routers as targets.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • rutos-device (GET /api/system/device/status, 30m): model, firmware and names as rutos_device_info;
  • rutos-system (GET /api/system/device/usage/status);
  • rutos-modems (GET /api/modems/status);
  • rutos-interfaces (GET /api/interfaces/status);
  • rutos-failover (GET /api/failover/status).
  • Deliverables: provider package, fixtures from anonymized recordings, dashboard, e2e test.

items.title: meraki-dashboard
items.text:
Cisco Meraki Dashboard API v1. Checked in November 2026 against the developer documentation and the official OpenAPI description (v1.75.1).

  • Auth: API key as Authorization: Bearer <key> (authorization).
  • Base URL: https://api.meraki.com/api/v1; regional variants api.meraki.ca, api.meraki.cn, api.meraki.in, api.gov-meraki.com (account param baseURL).
  • Rate limits (rate limit):
  • per organization: 10 requests per second, token bucket, with 10 more allowed in the first second (30 in two seconds), shared by every application of the organization: rate: 10/s, burst: 20, scoped by var:organizationId on the organization endpoints;
  • per source IP: 100 requests per second, shared by every client on the address: rate: 100/s per instance;
  • concurrency: not documented officially (10 per IP is community knowledge): concurrency: 10 per instance, marked assumed;
  • 429 with Retry-After, body {"errors": ["API rate limit exceeded for organization"]}; no quota headers.
  • Pagination: Link header (RFC 8288) with perPage; the startingAfter and endingBefore tokens are opaque, the rel=next link is followed (pagination).
  • Discovery chain: organizations -> organization-wide endpoints (one call for every device of an organization), networks only for _info labels.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • meraki-organizations (inventory, GET /organizations);
  • meraki-networks (forEach organizations, GET /organizations/{organizationId}/networks);
  • meraki-devices (GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices);
  • meraki-device-availabilities (GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/availabilities). It replaces devices/statuses, deprecated in October 2024 (deprecated operations);
  • meraki-appliance-uplink-statuses (GET /organizations/{organizationId}/appliance/uplink/statuses);
  • meraki-wireless-client-counts (GET /organizations/{organizationId}/wireless/clients/overview/byDevice, an enveloped list under items).
  • Deliverables: provider package, synthetic simulator (inventory generator sized by config), fixtures derived from the OpenAPI examples, dashboard, contract tests, and an e2e test run against a DevNet sandbox organization (November 2026, every template; the sandbox appliance reports no uplink, so the uplink metrics are validated against the simulator only).

items.title: aruba-central-classic
items.text:
HPE Aruba Networking Central (classic platform) REST API. Checked in November 2026 against the Aruba developer hub and the official pycentral SDK, then against a real Central account, read-only: every template, the token rotation and the quota headers.

  • Auth: OAuth access tokens valid 2 hours and rotating refresh tokens valid 15 days, implemented by the aruba_central_classic auth plugin (see 05-collection.md). Bootstrap: client ID and secret of an API Gateway application and the token pair downloaded from API Gateway > System Apps & Tokens (or My Apps & Tokens).
  • Base URL: regional API gateway (account param baseURL, required), for example https://apigw-eucentral3.central.arubanetworks.com; the README lists the clusters. A token only works on the gateway of its cluster.
  • Rate limits (usage and rate limits):
  • per account, per second: 7 calls (429 when exceeded);
  • per account, per day: the maximum of 5000 and the sum of 30 calls per Foundation device and 90 per Advanced device; resets at midnight GMT;
  • response headers X-RateLimit-Limit-day, X-RateLimit-Remaining-day, X-RateLimit-Limit-second, X-RateLimit-Remaining-second; no Retry-After documented;
  • token creation is limited to one per client ID every 30 minutes for the login and authorization-code APIs; the refresh API has no documented limit;
  • declared as kind: quota, period: day, resetAt: "00:00", timezone: UTC, max: auto (initialMax: 5000) with sync headers, plus kind: rate 7/s per account.
  • Pagination: offset / limit, maximum 1000 on the monitoring lists, total only with calculate_total=true.
  • Budget strategy: the daily quota is the binding constraint. List endpoints with 1000 items per page; no per-device endpoint; inventory jobs with long intervals. tapyr plan makes the cost visible.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • aruba-aps (GET /monitoring/v2/aps?calculate_client_count=true: the client count comes with the list, at no extra cost);
  • aruba-switches (GET /monitoring/v1/switches);
  • aruba-gateways (GET /monitoring/v1/gateways);
  • aruba-sites (inventory, GET /central/v2/sites).
  • Deliverables: provider package, synthetic simulator enforcing 7/s and the daily quota with headers, quota-tight scenario, dashboard, contract tests. No e2e test (no access).

items.title: Note on Aruba Central "new" (GreenLake-based)
items.text: The newer HPE Aruba Networking Central platform uses a different API surface and OAuth client credentials through HPE GreenLake. It will be a separate provider package (aruba-central), after v0.1.0. Its client-credentials auth should work with the declarative oauth2_client_credentials type, which is a good sign for the abstraction.

items.title: juniper-mist
items.text:
Juniper Mist cloud REST API. Checked in November 2026 against the Mist documentation and the Mist OpenAPI description (2610.1.0).

  • Auth: API token as Authorization: Token <key> (header auth with format: "Token {value}"). An organization token with a read-only role is recommended; a user token works too (Org API token).
  • Base URL: the API host of the cloud of the organization (account param baseURL, default https://api.mist.com), 12 regional hosts (endpoints by global region); the organization ID is the account param orgId.
  • Rate limits:
  • 5000 calls per hour, reset at the hourly boundary (API rate limiting, RESTful API overview);
  • counted per organization token, or for the whole user account with a user token, portal logins included;
  • 429 when exceeded; no Retry-After and no rate-limit headers documented; no per-second or concurrency limit documented;
  • declared as kind: quota, period: hour, timezone: UTC, max: 5000, scope: { by: [credential] }.
  • Pagination: limit (maximum 1000) and page, with the total in X-Page-Total (pagination); the package stops on a short page.
  • Budget strategy: organization-level statistics only, about 20 calls an hour for an organization of up to 1000 devices.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • mist-devices (GET /api/v1/orgs/{orgId}/stats/devices?type=all: access points, switches and gateways in one list);
  • mist-sites (GET /api/v1/orgs/{orgId}/stats/sites: device and client counts per site);
  • mist-alarms (GET /api/v1/orgs/{orgId}/alarms/count?distinct=severity&duration=1d).
  • Deliverables: provider package, synthetic simulator enforcing the hourly quota, scenarios, dashboard, contract test. No e2e test (no access).

items.title: cisco-thousandeyes
items.text:
Cisco ThousandEyes API v7. Checked in November 2026 against the rate limit documentation and the official SDKs (thousandeyes-sdk-python 7.0.110).

  • Auth: bearer token of a user (Authorization: Bearer <token>); the account group is the optional account param accountGroupId (the aid query parameter, omitted when unset: the default account group of the user).
  • Base URL: https://api.thousandeyes.com/v7 (account param baseURL).
  • Rate limits:
  • 240 requests a minute per organization, "one minute from the first request in a batch"; instant tests (24 a minute) and template deployments (10 a minute) have limits of their own, unused by the package;
  • X-Organization-Rate-Limit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset (the epoch of the next rollover) on every response; 429 when exceeded, no Retry-After; the documented example shows a limit of 20;
  • declared as kind: quota, period: minute, max: auto (initialMax: 240), scope: { by: [account] }, with the three sync headers: the reset header keeps the window on the one of the API (04-budget-engine.md, Header sync).
  • Pagination: _links.next in the body; without a time window, the latest round of every agent fits one page, which the package reads (and reports a next page in thousandeyes_network_results_truncated).
  • Budget strategy: one request per network test and run; about 10 requests a minute for 50 tests at the default 5 minutes.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • thousandeyes-tests (inventory, GET /tests);
  • thousandeyes-agents (GET /agents);
  • thousandeyes-network-results (GET /test-results/{testId}/network, one instance per enabled agent-to-server or agent-to-agent test, samples stamped with their round).
  • Deliverables: provider package, synthetic simulator enforcing the organization limit with its headers, scenarios, dashboard, contract test. No e2e test (no access).

items.title: unifi-site-manager
items.text:
UniFi Site Manager API v1. Checked in November 2026 against the Getting Started page, the OpenAPI description (Site Manager API 1.0.0) and the responses of a real account (read-only).

  • Auth: an API key of the UI account in the X-API-Key header (unifi.ui.com, Settings > API Keys, the Site Manager scope only); the key sees every console the account owns or administers.
  • Base URL: https://api.ui.com (account param baseURL).
  • Rate limits:
  • 10,000 requests a minute for the v1 stable release, 100 for Early Access endpoints (unused); 429 with Retry-After in seconds when exceeded; no quota header (checked on a real account);
  • the scope is not documented: declared as kind: rate, rate: 10000/m, scope: { by: [credential] };
  • the connector (/v1/connector/consoles/{id}/..., 100 requests a minute per console, which also accepts writes) is not used.
  • Pagination: an opaque cursor, pageSize and nextToken in the query, nextToken in the body (absent on the last page); on /v1/devices, a page counts consoles, each with all its devices. No maximum page size is documented.
  • Budget strategy: account-wide lists, no fan-out: 4 requests every 5 minutes and one every 15 minutes for up to 100 consoles.
  • Templates (metrics in the package README):
  • unifi-hosts (GET /v1/hosts);
  • unifi-sites (GET /v1/sites, one item per site and per WAN interface);
  • unifi-devices (GET /v1/devices);
  • unifi-isp-metrics (GET /v1/isp-metrics/5m?beginTimestamp=<now - 1h>, windows published about 30 minutes late, stamped with their start);
  • unifi-isp-metrics-hourly (GET /v1/isp-metrics/1h, optional).
  • Deliverables: provider package, synthetic simulator (the lists paginate themselves with a body cursor), scenarios, dashboard, contract test. No e2e test.

items.title: Provider package checklist (definition of done)
items.text:
• [ ] provider.yaml with every limit sourced (link in README) or marked as measured/assumed.
  • [ ] Job templates with estimate.pagesPerRun hints.
  • [ ] Simulator: routes, fixtures (synthetic or anonymized recordings), default, quota-tight and bad-day scenarios.
  • [ ] Contract tests passing (tapyr provider lint).
  • [ ] Dashboard in dashboards/.
  • [ ] Example Account and Job documents in examples/.
  • [ ] README: coverage, auth setup steps, limits with sources, validation status (real platform or simulator only), known caveats.
  • [ ] Metric naming reviewed: <provider_prefix>_<object>_<measure>_<unit>, base units, _info for descriptive attributes, no high-cardinality labels (no client MACs).
